 - People who ignore crashes, edge cases, loading states or performance.

 - Engineers who move slowly in a startup environment.

 - People who exaggerate impact without explaining their actual contribution.

 


LOCATION

This role is based in United States. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our United States office at least 3 days per week.  

 


LANGUAGE

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 


INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round


For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

jobs.title: Staff Electrical Engineer
jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION



Form's Advanced Product Development team is responsible for architecting and designing the next generation of our iron-air battery system — the cell, module, pack, and the support systems that keep them running reliably for decades in the field. We work ahead of our production programs, translating breakthrough electrochemistry and system requirements into electrical, controls, and test systems that can scale to high-volume manufacturing.



We are hiring a Staff Electrical Engineer to lead electrical hardware development for our next-generation battery program in Somerville, MA. You will own the design of control systems, power conversion, and test hardware for the next generation battery, and you will build and lead the electrical team that delivers it.



This is a hands-on individual contributor role with team leadership from day one. As the team grows, you will continue to drive technical progress while mentoring and growing the team



Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Lead electrical hardware development for control systems, power conversion, and test hardware, from architecture and requirements through build, bring-up, and validation.

 - Design and specify control enclosures: component selection, schematics, layout, wiring and harness documentation, and thermal management.

 - Define the power conversion approach, then select or design converters, protection, and power distribution for prototype and test systems.

 - Design control and safety systems, including sensors, interlocks, and instrumentation.

 - Make sure designs meet applicable codes and standards (NFPA 70/79, UL 508A, IEC), and champion lab and high-voltage safety.

 - Lead, mentor, and grow a team of electrical engineers: set technical direction, review designs, and own delivery against schedule.

 - Work with mechanical, test, and operations teams to turn product and test needs into electrical requirements.

 - Guide PLC programming, HMI development, and commissioning for the systems your team builds.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - B.S. in Electrical Engineering or a closely related field.

 - 8+ years of electrical hardware development, including control enclosure design and power conversion, in energy storage, EV, power electronics, industrial automation, or a similar field.

 - Proficiency with ECAD tools (e.g., AutoCAD Electrical, SolidWorks Electrical, EPLAN).

 - Working knowledge of NFPA 70/79, UL 508A, and IEC standards for industrial control and power equipment.

 - Experience leading engineers, as a technical lead or manager, with a track record of delivering high-quality hardware on schedule.

 - PLC programming (e.g., Rockwell, Siemens, Beckhoff) and HMI design.

 - Functional safety experience (ISO 13849, IEC 62061).

 - Familiarity with battery and energy storage standards (UL 9540, UL 1973).

 - Comfort building, bringing up, and debugging hardware hands-on in the lab.

 - Clear communication with technicians, engineers, and leadership.
   

#LI-Onsite



Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here. 



When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed. 



To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.




If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.

Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will never solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.

jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Physical AI
jobs.description:
Apptronik is a human-centered robotics company developing AI-powered robots to support humanity in every facet of life. Our flagship humanoid robot, Apollo, is built to collaborate thoughtfully with people, starting with critical industries such as manufacturing and logistics, with future applications in healthcare, the home, and beyond.

We operate at the cutting edge of Applied AI, applying our expertise across the full robotics stack to solve some of society's most important problems. You will join a team dedicated to bringing Apollo to market at scale, tackling the complex challenges like safety, commercialization, and mass production to change the world for the better.

JOB SUMMARY

We are looking for a highly technical Staff or Principal Technical Program Manager to lead the programs that train Apollo's AI. This role owns the full physical AI training lifecycle: the compute infrastructure we train on, the data engine that feeds it, the pretraining, mid-training, and post-training runs that produce our models, and the path that takes those models onto robots in the field.

You will operate as a technical peer to research and infrastructure leadership, not a schedule keeper. You will set the strategy for how training programs are planned and resourced, own the build-out and utilization of our cloud and on-premises GPU capacity, and turn research goals into executable plans with clear gates and decisions. As the function grows, you will define the program management practices that let Apptronik train and ship models faster than anyone else in physical AI.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES or KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES

• Compute Strategy & Infrastructure: Own the strategy and execution for Apptronik's training compute across cloud and on-premises GPUs. Drive capacity forecasting, build-vs-buy decisions, vendor and cloud partnerships, cluster bring-up, and the utilization, cost, and allocation of compute across research teams.

• Training Program Execution: Run pretraining, mid-training, fine-tuning, and distillation efforts as disciplined programs. Define compute budgets, data freeze dates, checkpoint and evaluation gates, and go/no-go criteria, and lead the response when a run diverges or infrastructure fails.

• Data Engine: Own the program that turns model needs into training data, spanning teleoperation, human demonstration, and simulation. Translate research requirements into collection plans, quality standards, and SOPs, and scale data throughput with the pipelines and storage behind it.

• Evaluation & Model Release: Establish a rigorous evaluation and release process across simulation and real robots. Drive statistically sound benchmarks, regression gates, and clear promotion criteria so release decisions rest on evidence, not demos.

• Deployment & Fleet Learning: Own the path from trained checkpoint to on-robot inference, including model optimization for edge hardware and integration with software, controls, and firmware. Build the loop that brings fleet data back into post-training and safely rolls out improved policies.

• Ownership: Own program execution end to end. Set strategic direction, identify resource requirements, and be accountable for delivering on company goals and roadmap. Challenge assumptions at the org level and foster a results-driven culture.

• Communication: Proactively communicate program status, risks, trade-offs, and decisions to executive stakeholders. Make compute, data, and model trade-offs legible to leadership and clearly articulate requirements, goals, and milestones across teams.

• Leadership & Mentorship: Mentor TPMs and engineers, and define the frameworks, tooling, and operating rhythms that let research move fast without losing rigor. Raise the technical bar of the program management function.

SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS

• Large-Scale Training Programs — Deep experience leading programs for large model training, including pretraining, mid-training, fine-tuning, and distillation. Fluency in how runs are planned, resourced, monitored, and recovered when they fail.

• GPU Compute & ML Infrastructure — Hands-on understanding of GPU clusters across cloud and on-premises environments, including schedulers, distributed training, high-speed interconnects, and storage. Experience driving capacity planning, procurement, and cluster bring-up.

• Hands-On Technical Depth — Ability to read training code, interpret loss curves and evaluation results, and diagnose data and infrastructure issues alongside the team. Comfortable with Python and a modern framework such as PyTorch or JAX.

• Robot Learning Data — Experience with the data that drives physical AI: teleoperation, demonstration capture, simulation and synthetic data, annotation, and quality control at scale.

• Evaluation Rigor — Experience building evaluation frameworks and release criteria for ML models, ideally spanning simulation and real-world testing.

• Edge Deployment — Familiarity with taking models from training to on-device inference, including optimization for embedded and edge AI hardware.

• Vendor & Partner Management — Proven success managing cloud providers, hardware vendors, and data partners, including negotiating capacity and resolving cross-org dependencies.

• Research Program Leadership — Ability to plan around research uncertainty using experiments, decision points, and gates rather than fixed deliverables, while holding infrastructure and data work to firm commitments.

• Influence in Resource-Constrained Environments — Proven ability to allocate scarce compute and data across competing teams, align research, engineering, and executive leadership, and make hard prioritization calls.

• Strategic Thinking — Ability to translate company strategy into compute, data, and model roadmaps, and influence those roadmaps through data-driven insight.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, or a related technical field required

• 10+ years of experience in technical program management, ML engineering, or ML infrastructure, including leading large-scale training or compute programs at a senior, staff, or principal level

• Preferred: Experience at a frontier AI lab, hyperscaler, or robotics foundation model company

• Preferred: Experience standing up or scaling GPU clusters or data center capacity

• Preferred: Direct experience with robot learning, vision-language-action models, or large-scale robot data programs

• Preferred: Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer

• Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times

• Vision to read printed materials and a computer screen

• Hearing and speech to communicate

The salary range for this position is $240,000 - $280,000

*This is a direct hire.  Please, no outside Agency solicitations.

jobs.title: Clinical Pharmacist - Ambulatory Care
jobs.description:
Akido builds AI-powered doctors. Akido is the first AI-native care provider, combining cutting-edge technology with a nationwide medical network to address America’s physician shortage and make exceptional healthcare universal. Its AI empowers doctors to deliver faster, more accurate, and more compassionate care.

Serving 500K+ patients across California, Rhode Island, and New York, Akido offers primary and specialty care in 26 specialties—from serving unhoused communities in Los Angeles to ride-share drivers in New York.

Founded in 2015 (YC W15), Akido is expanding its risk-bearing care models and scaling ScopeAI, its breakthrough clinical AI platform. Read more about Akido’s $60M Series B. More info at Akidolabs.com.

The Opportunity

The Clinical Pharmacist provides ambulatory pharmaceutical care services within the Rhode Island Primary Care Physicians Corporation (RIPCPC) ACO. The pharmacist is embedded within primary care practices and collaborates as part of the interdisciplinary care team to provide evidence-based, patient-centered medication management focused on optimizing medication regimens, improving chronic disease outcomes, and reducing avoidable healthcare utilization.

This position supports a new pharmacist-led COPD population health program focused on high-risk patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, including transitions of care management, medication optimization, inhaler education, adherence support, and early exacerbation intervention. In addition to COPD-focused responsibilities, the pharmacist will support broader ambulatory care pharmacy services and organizational quality initiatives based on program needs and operational priorities.

This is a newly funded program being built from the ground up. The pharmacist in this role won't inherit an established workflow — they'll help design it: the collaborative practice agreement scope, the clinical protocols, how high-risk patients are identified and followed, and how outcomes are measured. This is an unusual opportunity to shape a program rather than staff one, with the support of an experienced pharmacy team, nurse care managers, and the Chief Medical Officer.

The Clinical Pharmacist ensures the safe, effective, evidence-based, and cost-conscious use of medications while promoting high-quality patient care. The pharmacist also serves as a medication and drug information resource for patients, providers, and interdisciplinary care team members.

What you’ll do

Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Functions as the medication expert on the interdisciplinary care team.

• Reconciles and assesses medication regimens for adherence, safety, effectiveness, and optimization of therapy to achieve desired clinical outcomes.

• Provides evidence-based, patient-centered medication therapy recommendations in collaboration with providers and care team members.

• Delivers chronic disease state management services with emphasis on COPD guideline-directed therapy, inhaler technique education, adherence monitoring, and mitigation of medication access barriers.

• Identifies and engages high-risk COPD patients through population health and care management platforms, including patients with recent emergency department visits, hospital admissions, or readmissions.

• Conducts transitions of care medication evaluations following acute care encounters and coordinates follow-up care with primary care teams and other providers as appropriate.

• Educates patients on medications, disease states, self-management strategies, and recognition of early COPD exacerbation symptoms to support timely intervention and reduce avoidable acute care utilization.

• Practices within established collaborative practice agreement(s) consistent with services delineated within the agreement.

• Collaborates with providers, patients, payers, and care management teams to ensure high-quality, cost-effective care.

• Participates in the development, implementation, and evaluation of quality improvement initiatives and population health programs.

• Contributes to achievement of contractual and organizational quality goals, including but not limited to comprehensive medication reviews, medication adherence outreach, transitions of care initiatives, and gaps in care closure.

• Documents all patient encounters and interventions within the electronic health record and other required platforms while maintaining timely communication with interdisciplinary team members.

• Assists in the collection, tracking, and reporting of program outcomes and quality metrics including utilization, engagement, and clinical outcomes.

• Develops and delivers presentations related to quality metrics, clinical initiatives, and disease state management topics.

• Participates in the development of new pharmacy services, workflows, and best practices supporting ambulatory and population health initiatives.

• Provides coverage and support for additional ambulatory clinical pharmacy services and team initiatives based on departmental needs.

Who you are

Required Qualifications:

• Experience independently managing drug therapy in an ambulatory or primary care setting, including initiating, adjusting, and discontinuing medications in collaboration with providers (e.g., under a collaborative practice agreement or similar delegated authority).

• Comfortable working at the top of your license — confident making independent clinical decisions without requiring physician sign-off at every step.

• Maintains current unrestricted pharmacist licensure in accordance with the Rhode Island Board of Registration in Pharmacy.

• Must have advanced training and experience relevant to chronic disease management meeting one of the following qualifications: Successfully completed certification from the Board of Pharmaceutical Specialties or completed an ASHP-accredited residency program in the area of practice. If the residency program is not in the area of practice, the pharmacist shall complete a continuing education certificate program. Holds a PharmD degree and has two (2) years of professional experience. Holds a Bachelor of Science in Pharmacy degree and has three (3) years of professional experience.

• Practices pharmacy in accordance with laws, rules, and regulations of the Rhode Island Board of Registration in Pharmacy, Department of Public Health, U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and Drug Enforcement Administration, as well as established departmental policies and procedures.

Preferred Education, Additional Qualifications, and Experience:

• Ambulatory care, population health, or chronic disease management experience preferred.

• Experience managing respiratory disease states including COPD and asthma preferred (e.g., pulmonary or asthma clinic background, inhaler technique education).

• Completion of an ASHP-accredited residency (PGY-1 and/or PGY-2, particularly ambulatory care) preferred.

• Experience working as part of interdisciplinary care teams.

• Experience supporting transitions of care following hospital discharge or ER visits.

• Self-motivated and comfortable helping build and shape a new clinical program.

• Experience utilizing electronic health records, population health platforms, and reporting tools.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications including Word, Excel, Outlook, and web-based systems.

Benefits:

• Health benefits include medical, dental, vision, and others

• Company paid health reimbursement arrangement (HRA)

• 401K match eligibility at 1 year

• Paid Time Off, paid holidays

• Life insurance

Physical Demands:

• Mostly sedentary work duties require exerting up to thirty pounds of force occasionally and/or small amounts of force frequently. Sedentary work typically involves sitting most of the time but may involve walking or standing for brief periods.

• Requires visual acuity and manual dexterity sufficient to operate a computer and other standard office equipment.

• Workspace may vary depending on provider office setting and assigned practice location.

• Travel between facilities, provider offices, and practice sites is required.

Salary range

$125,000—$135,000 USD

Akido Labs, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer, and we encourage qualified applicants of every background, ability, and life experience to contact us about appropriate employment opportunities.

jobs.title: Maintenance Planner
jobs.description:
With a strategy centered on people and sustainability, Braskem is engaged in contributing to the value chain to strengthen the Circular Economy. Braskem’s 9,000 team members dedicate themselves every day to improving people's lives through sustainable solutions in chemicals and plastics. With its corporate DNA rooted in innovation, Braskem offers a comprehensive portfolio of plastic resins and chemical products for diverse industries, such as food packaging, construction, manufacturing, automotive, agribusiness, health and hygiene, and more. With 40 industrial units in Brazil, the United States, Mexico, and Germany, Braskem exports its products to clients in over 70 countries.

Braskem America is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Braskem S.A. headquartered in Philadelphia. The company is the leading producer of polypropylene in the United States, with six production plants located in Texas, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia, as well as an Innovation and Technology Center in Pittsburgh and a New Renewable Innovation Center in Lexington, which focuses on leveraging groundbreaking developments in biotechnology and chemical catalysis. For more information, visit www.braskem.com/usa.

Department: Maintenance

Location: La Porte, TX

Travel Involved: Less than 5%

Job Type: Full-time

Description:

This role is focused on the mechanical planning aspects of the Braskem maintenance work process (MPE).  A successful candidate will provide a detailed plan, in the form of a job package, for each assigned task, identifying the appropriate resources required for execution.  Planning involves receiving a notification, converting it to a work order, scoping the job in the field, identifying required materials, estimating manpower and equipment, and creating an effective job sequence.  This information is used with SAP to develop a work schedule and ultimately for executing the work.  The plans are to be developed and written so that maintenance technicians or contractors can complete the job safely, efficiently, and cost-effectively. The jobs will be planned in SAP with the logic necessary for the scheduler to tie tasks or resources together into a coherent schedule.  The planner also creates task lists for routine work orders and Preventative Maintenance (PM) activities.  In addition, the Planner refines and improves existing plans using feedback forms.

Key Responsibilities Include:

• Review the group of notifications prioritized by the PMC daily for planning.

• Process work notifications and work orders properly, ensuring status codes are correct.

• Discuss and understand the notification scope, interacting with the notification issuer and/or other key stakeholders.

• Create Work Orders using appropriate codes for the type of work.

• Visit the job site and scope out the job by taking pictures, creating drawings, and assembling a bill of materials.

• Attach necessary pictures and documents to the plan.

• Enter plans into the work orders by developing a well-defined scope of work, including all necessary steps required to complete the work order in the safest and most efficient manner.

• Ensure maintenance and production personnel understand the work scope by providing clear Work Order instructions and by discussing plans with stakeholders.

• Create task lists in SAP for future work.

• Review existing task lists to ensure applicability and quality for future use.

• Request materials, parts, and services as necessary for maintenance work.

• Monitor the receipt of materials with the storeroom so work can be scheduled in a timely manner.

• Ensure orders and materials are appropriately expedited when necessary.

• Send procurement and warehouse requests for rush orders to expedite materials for priority work.

• Inform engineers of Add/Change/Delete needs for spare parts that must be modified in inventory. Also inform when parts aren’t tied to equipment BOM in SAP.

• Provide updates on the planning status and backlog as required.

• Ensure plans meet the timing needs of the operating units. This is achieved through constant communication with the PMC and other stakeholders.

• Assemble job packages so the maintenance supervisors/craftsmen can pull them at the appropriate time.

• Review feedback from Maintenance Technicians, Engineers, etc. on the plans.

• Update task lists based on feedback and other knowledge about the work.

• Drive continual improvement of job plans for safety, quality, accuracy, etc

• Identify repeat work, rework, and recurring failures and alert other functions within the MPE process.

• Support emergency work as needed.

• Participate in managing the work order backlog by reviewing backlog and planning lists to identify, eliminate, and redefine duplicate orders.

• Work with the contractor administrator by issuing requisitions for outside contractors on planned jobs so he can issue them a PO.

• Support issuing PO’s or creating SES’s when needed.

Requirements:

• Must be able to be on call periodically.

• Must be available during off hours to support unexpected plant equipment issues and downtime.

• Must have a minimum of 5 years applicable industry experience.

• High school diploma is required; higher education credentials are preferred (University, Technical College, Trade School, etc.).

• Must have a strong plant aptitude

• Proficient computer skills required

• Must be extremely familiar with SAP, Maximo, and Primavera.

• Must be able to effectively plan work in SAP

• Previous experience as a planner is beneficial.

What we offer

At Braskem, we offer more than just a competitive pay package. Our total rewards package includes a wide range of benefits you need for every stage of your life. Our benefits include:

• Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefits

• Retirement Benefits

• Maternity and Paternity Leave

• Life Insurance

• Short- and Long-Term Disability Insurance

• Teladoc

• A wide range of voluntary benefits like Pet Insurance, Legal and ID Theft Insurance

• Flexible work schedules like 9/80 schedules for eligible team members

Depending on qualifications, the successful candidate may be offered a position at a more appropriate level and/or ladder.

Candidates must be currently eligible to work in the United States without the need for any type of sponsorship now or in the future. Braskem is committed to equal employment opportunity and providing reasonable accommodations to qualified candidates and employees according to applicable law. We value and encourage diversity and solicit applications from all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, gender, sex, age, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, medical condition, military and veteran status, gender identity or expression, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. If you require reasonable accommodation as part of the application process, please contact the Talent Acquisition team.

jobs.title: Principal, Talent Acquisition & Mobility Analytics
jobs.description:
At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

This role will be based in Sunnyvale, Mountain View, San Francisco, Bellevue, Carpinteria, Chicago, Detroit, New York, Omaha or Washington, D.C.

LinkedIn's Talent Acquisition & Mobility (TA&M) Analytics team works closely with leaders to deliver insights, conducts research, and builds products that help them make more informed decisions that drive impact across TA&M and the business.

We are looking for a Principal to build the next generation of analytics and AI-enabled solutions. Working within an embedded TA&M analytics team alongside talent and business leaders, you will create reliable, reusable tools, applications, and models that make insights accessible, enable scenario planning, and inform decisions. Your work will help leaders understand performance drivers, anticipate business demand, and improve team operations to maximize business value.

To do this work, you will need strong technical development skills, applied analytics expertise, and sound statistical judgment, along with experience using AI and modern development tools. You can translate complex business needs into practical solutions and collaborate with others to take them from concept through design, development, testing, and implementation.

You are a curious, resourceful problem-solver who learns quickly and thrives as the work evolves. As AI reshapes how we work, you are ready to explore new tools and technologies, respond to shifting priorities, and grow beyond familiar approaches. You bring an open mind and a practical focus on turning new possibilities into meaningful business impact.

Responsibilities

Analytics Solutions Development

• Build analytical applications, tools, and models from requirements through development, testing, implementation, and continuous improvement, integrating data and AI to solve complex business problems.
• Use AI and modern development tools to accelerate development, simplify analytics, automate manual work, and improve access to and use of information.
• Build solutions that turn research findings into practical tools for monitoring performance, measuring outcomes, and informing ongoing decisions.

Technical Development

• Design and maintain data models, calculations, and structures for reporting, applications, and AI solutions using SQL, Python, cloud data platforms, and modern development environments.
• Partner with data engineering to ensure reliable, consistent, appropriately governed data.
• Apply documentation, testing, version control, and maintenance practices while modernizing reporting and analytics tools and preserving critical business capabilities.

Advanced Analytics

• Apply statistical analysis, forecasting, predictive modeling, and other methods to identify performance drivers, forecast outcomes, and evaluate business scenarios.
• Use AI-assisted tools to develop, test, and validate models, assessing accuracy, assumptions, limitations, and business relevance.

Business Partnership

• Partner with TA&M leaders to translate business challenges into clear requirements and recommend solutions based on data availability, feasibility, and impact.
• Collaborate with research, analytics, engineering, and business teams to build adoptable, maintainable solutions.
• Communicate technical concepts and findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences, helping stakeholders adopt new tools and ways of working.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Applied Statistics, Analytics, Computer Science, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, or related field AND 7+ years of experience in people analytics, data analytics, consulting, finance, analytics, process management, program management, or similar field, OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

• Master's degree in Applied Statistics, Analytics, Computer Science, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, or related field AND 5+ years of experience in people analytics, data analytics, consulting, finance, analytics, process management, program management, or similar field, OR Doctorate in Applied Statistics, Analytics, Computer Science, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Industrial/Organizational Psychology, or related field AND 3+ years of experience in people analytics, data analytics, consulting, finance, analytics, process management, program management, or similar field, OR equivalent experience.
• 5+ years of experience using data visualization tools, such as Power BI, Tableau, Visier, or Domo.
• Proficiency in SQL, Python, or comparable programming languages, with experience working with complex data, analytical models, and modern cloud data platforms, such as Databricks.
• Experience independently designing, developing, and deploying analytical applications, models, AI-enabled solutions, or automated workflows that address complex business problems.
• Experience with statistical modeling, forecasting, predictive analytics, scenario modeling, or other advanced analytical methods.
• Experience translating business requirements into analytical solutions, working across technical disciplines, and communicating findings to technical and nontechnical audiences.
• Experience in Talent Acquisition, Talent Management, People Analytics, workforce planning, or operational analytics.

Suggested Skills

• Stakeholder Management
• Analytics
• Communication

LinkedIn is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices.

The pay range for this role is $148,000 to $243,000. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience, certifications, and specific work location. This may be different in other locations due to differences in the cost of labor.

The total compensation package for this position may also include annual performance bonus, stock, benefits and/or other applicable incentive compensation plans. For more information, visit https://careers.linkedin.com/benefits.

Equal Opportunity Statement

We seek candidates with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. LinkedIn considers qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, sex, gender expression or identity, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

LinkedIn is committed to offering an inclusive and accessible experience for all job seekers, including individuals with disabilities. Our goal is to foster an inclusive and accessible workplace where everyone has the opportunity to be successful.

If you need a Reasonable Accommodation to search for a job opening, apply for a position, or participate in the interview process, connect with us and describe the specific Accommodation requested for a disability-related limitation.

Fill out an Accommodation request here: https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/b660a0327d044969abfd7a4e73d15c36

A request for an accommodation will be responded to within three business days. However, non-disability related requests, such as following up on an application, will not receive a response.

LinkedIn will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by LinkedIn, or (c) consistent with LinkedIn's legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.title: Staff Mechanical Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Staff Mechanical Engineer to help advance the development, testing, and production of Kaleidos, our portable, helium-cooled nuclear microreactor. With our first reactor built and production design underway, you'll join our Turbomachinery team, working alongside a multidisciplinary group developing critical hardware for the reactor's power generation and primary cooling systems.

Your work will span mechanical design, structural analysis, component development, materials selection, and hardware integration for complex mechanical and rotating systems. You'll provide technical leadership across engineering challenges involving high-speed machinery, precision assemblies, bearings, seals, and components operating under demanding thermal and mechanical conditions. This is an opportunity to drive critical design decisions, solve complex hardware problems, and help bring Kaleidos from development through testing and into commercial deployment.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Lead the mechanical design and development of complex components and assemblies supporting Kaleidos' turbomachinery and power generation systems.

 - Own critical hardware designs from concept development and engineering analysis through manufacturing, testing, and production.

 - Perform and guide engineering analyses involving structural integrity, mechanical loads, thermal effects, vibration, and component performance.

 - Establish design requirements, evaluate technical tradeoffs, and drive engineering decisions involving materials, manufacturing methods, tolerances, and mechanical interfaces.

 - Collaborate with turbomachinery, thermal, fluid systems, manufacturing, and test engineers to resolve complex multidisciplinary challenges and optimize system performance.

 - Provide technical direction during prototype development, hardware fabrication, assembly, and testing to validate design requirements and engineering assumptions.

 - Lead root cause investigations, evaluate hardware failures, and develop solutions to improve mechanical performance, reliability, and manufacturability.

 - Drive design reviews, mentor engineers, and establish engineering best practices to improve technical quality and execution across the team.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related field from an accredited institution.

 - 8+ years of relevant professional experience in mechanical design, hardware development, or related engineering disciplines.

 - Deep understanding of mechanical engineering fundamentals, including mechanics of materials, structural analysis, machine design, and material behavior.

 - Extensive experience designing complex mechanical components and assemblies using 3D CAD software and producing detailed engineering drawings.

 - Experience applying advanced engineering calculations, simulation tools, or analytical methods to evaluate mechanical designs, structural integrity, and component performance.

 - Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), and design for manufacturability.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead complex mechanical design efforts, make critical technical decisions, and resolve challenging engineering problems across multidisciplinary teams.


DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related field.

 - Experience designing hardware for turbomachinery, rotating equipment, propulsion systems, or other high-performance mechanical systems.

 - Experience with bearings, seals, shafts, housings, precision assemblies, or high-speed rotating machinery.

 - Experience with finite element analysis (FEA), vibration analysis, fatigue, rotordynamics, or thermal-mechanical analysis.

 - Experience designing components for high-temperature, high-pressure, or other demanding operating environments.

 - Hands-on experience leading hardware development through fabrication, assembly, prototyping, testing, and production.

 - Experience with engineering tools such as Siemens NX, ANSYS, or similar CAD and analysis software.


ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

 - Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as necessary to accomplish our mission.

 - Must work 100% onsite at El Segundo HQ.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Nuclear Engineering Certificate Program: 100% covered educational program with Penn State University, for eligible employees, to rapidly upscale into nuclear.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s full-time new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.

The best of today’s advanced reactor builders don’t wait for job postings. They join the winning team. If that’s you, contact us directly for immediate opportunities: recruiting@radiantnuclear.com.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

This position involves access to technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant’s capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls.

jobs.title: Sr/Lead Validation Engineer
jobs.description:
The field of gene therapy is growing rapidly and Genezen is here to meet the exacting needs of our clients. We provide process development, produce GMP viral vectors, and provide cell transduction for gene and cell therapy clinical trials and are proud to be a part of the process that leads to new cures.

WORKING AT GENEZEN

Many people have worked in environments where you feel like just another nameless part of an enormous machine. Genezen is different. We want our employees to be innovative, collaborative problem solvers who are dedicated to meeting the challenges of working at a fast-growing company. We are dedicated to empowering our employees to be their best and making Genezen a rewarding place to work. Every employee contributes to the success of the company and you can be part of that team.

JOB SUMMARY

The Sr/Lead Validation Engineer is responsible for leading, managing and executing validation and qualification activities to ensure equipment, facilities, utilities, systems and processes comply with applicable regulatory requirements, industry standards and Genezen policies and procedures. The role provides technical leadership and oversight of the validation lifecycle in support and completion of MSAT & Validation project milestones as well as manufacturing support. The incumbent is also responsible for representing the Validation department during regulatory inspections and client audits.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Lead and coordinate validation and qualification activities.

• Develop, implement and maintain the site Validation Master Plan.

• Establish validation strategies, policies, procedures in compliance with regulatory requirements.

• Protocol generation, execution support, data analysis, report generation and approval for various installation, operational and performance qualification activities.

• Review and approve qualification documentation on behalf of the validation department and support the generation and implementation of validation programs.

• Ensure documentation and performance of qualification activities is scientifically sound, traceable, risk based and compliant with policies and procedures, industry standards and regulatory guidance.

• Establish cleaning validation strategies, acceptance criteria and sampling methodologies.

• Support environmental qualification and contamination control strategies.

• Support execution of APS on the fill lines.

• Support requalification of facilities, utilities and equipment where necessary.

• Support computer systems validation activities for equipment, facilities, utilities systems.

• Lead/support investigations into protocol nonconformances, deviations, investigations, root cause analysis, CAPA and change control activities.

• Establish and maintain validation standards, standard operating procedures and templates related to validation practices.

• Support the execution and generation of formal risk assessments related to qualification.

• Ensure monitoring and periodic review programs are established and maintained.

• Identify opportunities to improve validation processes, drive continuous improvement, reduce execution timelines, and increase operational efficiency while maintaining compliance.

• Support data integrity assessments and data integrity principles/program.

• Support internal audits, regulatory inspections and client audits

SPECIAL WORK REQUIREMENTS

• Fully onsite position

• Adaptability required as work schedule may change based on business needs

• Criminal background check required

• Other duties as assigned

EDUCATION/CERTIFCATIONS/LICENSES

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Biotechnology, Biological Sciences, or a related technical discipline.

Essential

ON-THE-JOB EXPERIENCE

8+ years of validation experience

Essential

Experience working in clean room environments.

Essential

Experience with aseptic processing and sterilization techniques.

Essential

Experience with validation lifecycle management and continued process verification.

Essential

Strong working knowledge of GxP regulations including 21 CFR Part 11 & 210/211, EU GMP Annex 1, 11 & 15, data integrity guidances, ICH guidelines with the ability to assess compliance risks.

Essential

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

Proven experience with equipment qualification, cleaning validation and facility/utility qualification.

Essential

Ability to work well with diverse groups in a matrix-style, growing, safety focused organization.

Essential

Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Visio, with the ability to develop technical documentation, analyze data, and create process flow diagrams.

Essential

Demonstrated ability to effectively manage competing priorities, adapt to changing business needs, and meet challenging deadlines in a fast-paced environment while maintaining quality, compliance, and adherence to project timelines.

Essential

Ability to work collaboratively as part of cross-functional teams maintaining effective communication with project team members to achieve project objectives including effectively reporting project activity in a clear and concise manner.

Essential

Strong interpersonal and communication skills, both verbal and written, with demonstrated experience preparing technical documents

Essential

Able to access crawl spaces and use ladders to access equipment.

Essential

COMPENSATION RANGE

The anticipated annual salary range for the Sr/Lead Validation Engineer position is $120,000-$150,000.  Actual annual salary and level will be determined based on relevant experience, skills and education.

Work Environment

• Regularly sit for long periods of time

• Able to access crawl spaces and use ladders to access equipment

Movement

• Frequently required to stand; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms

• Occasionally required to walk; climb or balance; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl

Lifting

• Frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds

• Rarely lift and/or move up to 25 pounds

Vision

• Frequently utilize close vision and the ability to adjust focus

Communication

• Frequently required to communicate by talking, hearing, using telephone and e-mail

GENEZEN'S CURES VALUE-BASED COMPETENCIES

Committed to Science
We are committed to scientific excellence, staying current with industry developments, making data-driven decisions, and pursuing innovation to advance healthcare.

Urgency in action for the patients
We operate with urgency and a commitment to delivering timely treatments to patients by accelerating our partners' programs.

Resilience & Grit in operations
We are committed to overcoming challenges, learning from failures, and persistently striving for success.

Execute with Excellence & Integrity
We are dedicated to delivering quality results and upholding ethical principals.

Solutions driven for our partners
We are committed to being a proactive, collaborative, creative and open-minded partner.

GENEZEN'S BENEFITS

• Paid vacation days, amount based on tenure

• Paid sick time

• 10 observed holidays + 2 floating holiday + 1 volunteer day

• 401(k) plan with company match up to 6% of salary

• Share Appreciation Rights

• Choice of several healthcare plans

• FSA and HSA programs

• Dental & vision care

• Employer-paid basic term life/personal accident insurance

• Voluntary disability, universal life/personal accident insurance

• Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance

ADDITIONAL DETAILS

• Nothing in the job description for this role restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

• This position requires a criminal background check.

• Genezen is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

• Genezen participates in EVerify.

• Genezen is interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States; however, we are not able to sponsor visas.

Genezen has operates two locations: one in Fishers, Indiana and the second in Lexington, Massachusetts.

Fishers is a suburb of Indianapolis. Fishers was named the #1 place to live in the US by Money Magazine in 2017 for its livability, safety and entrepreneurship. Fishers is one of the fastest growing communities in Indiana and is dedicated to supporting a high quality of life for all its residents. Nearby Indianapolis is home to professional and college sports teams, the Indy 500, a growing art community and the world’s largest children’s museum--to name just a few reasons why this area is a great place to live.

Lexington, Massachusetts, located just northwest of Boston, is renowned as a historic suburb with a rich cultural heritage. It boasts picturesque New England charm, tree-lined streets, and a vibrant community. Known for its pivotal role in the American Revolution, Lexington offers visitors and residents alike a blend of historical landmarks, modern amenities, and a strong sense of community pride.

jobs.title: Manager, Physical Security Operations Center
jobs.description:
The Role

The Security Operations Center (SOC) Manager will be responsible for managing a team of security professionals, ensuring the effective and efficient operations of physical security systems, maintaining the safety and security of our operation, ensuring compliance with regulatory standards, and managing business continuity in cases of disruptions. The successful candidate will be expected to develop and implement security programs, incident response procedures, develop and update security policies and procedures and communicate with internal and external partners, as necessary. The ideal SOC Manager is a process-driven individual that has a passion for analysis, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration.

Schedule & Work Location

• This is an on-site, position based in Mundelein, IL. The Physical Security Operations Manager oversees a team supporting first, second, and third shifts and must maintain the flexibility to regularly adjust and rotate their work schedule across all shifts. Schedule adjustments may include mornings, evenings, overnights, weekends, and holidays based on business and team needs.

Responsibilities

• Oversee the day-to-day operations of the 24/7 Security Operations Center and help with managing the physical security systems of the organization including Video, Access Control and Alarm systems.

• Supervise and train Security Operations Center staff, maintain staff scheduling and conduct performance evaluations.

• Assist staff with centrally coordinating and supporting field response to all disruptions: security incidents, compliance issues, health & life safety events, site & infrastructure issues, and natural disasters.

• Continuously monitor the environment, analyze risk, and provide situational awareness to the organization. Performs risk assessments, team member escorts, emergency response and regular remote assessments to identify security and safety hazards and policy violations.

• Communicates incidents to employees and executive leadership, using clear and concise written and verbal communications.

• Provides operational support, maintenance management, and ticket troubleshooting for all security related systems including CCTV, access control, alarms, safes, mobile tracking technologies.

• Assist with building a robust audit program to ensure regulatory compliance and oversees its execution by Security Operations Center staff.

• Ensures Security Operations staff are coordinating all service calls for security related equipment through field response vendor network.

• Build incident management protocols and facilitate case management processes for incidents.

• Assist in developing and building a robust business continuity program and overseeing it’s execution by Security Operations Center staff.

• Partner with key business partners internally to define and implement processes and standard work for the security operations function, including security playbook development, emergency operation plans, and other business continuity plans.

• Works with the Security Operations Center staff to liaise with local law enforcement and other first responders during incidents and provide incident notification during events.

• Build a training curriculum on systems in use to provide proper guidance, training and certification for Security Operations staff.

• Work with leadership to identify and implement enhancements in Security Operations Center processes and systems.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent work experience required.

• Minimum seven years of progressively responsible and relevant work experience.

• Minimum five years of experience in a managerial role required.

• Certifications in Physical Security Systems preferred.

• Experience using CCTV and alarm monitoring software in coordination with a communications center or Security Operations Center.

• Demonstrated knowledge of security systems for access control, CCTV systems, badging systems, alarm monitoring systems, mobile surveillance systems and GPS systems.

• Experience or familiarity with corporate intelligence, military intelligence or government intelligence agencies desired but not needed.

• Available to work all shifts and comfortable rotating through all shifts 24/7/365 and willing to assist when short staffed.

Skills

• Ability to effectively communicate verbally or in writing clearly and concisely while in stressful situations.

• Strong Leadership and team management experience.

• Demonstrates clear problem solving and decision-making abilities.

• Comfortable working with ambiguity.

• Adapts and thrives in a demanding, fast-paced environment.

• Operates with a high level of professionalism and integrity, including dealing with confidential information.

• Possesses a high level of critical thinking.

• Effective communication and interpersonal skills.

• Must understand and comply with the rules, regulations, policies, and procedures of Green Thumb.

Additional Requirements

• Must pass all required background checks.

• Must be and remain compliant with all legal or company regulations for working in the industry.

• Must possess a valid driver’s license.

• Must be at a minimum 21 years of age.

• Must be approved by state badging agency to work in cannabis industry.

The pay range is competitive and based on experience, qualifications, and/or location of the role. Positions may be eligible for a discretionary annual incentive program driven by organization and individual performance.

Green Thumb Pay Range

$110,000—$130,000 USD

jobs.description:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



THE ROLE

We're hiring an attorney to be the day-to-day legal partner to the teams building and securing our platform. You'll sit with Product and Engineering from design through launch, and you'll counsel Security, Compliance, Capacity, and the product and engineering teams on security including how what we commit to customers and how security and resilience run through our compute and infrastructure supply chain.

At Baseten, commercial and product are nearly one and the same. What we sell is inference: compute, orchestration, deployment, and optimization delivered as the production backbone for our customers' products. That means the security of the platform is the product. Our customers run their most sensitive workloads on us, and the questions Product, Engineering, and Security bring to Legal are commercial questions and engineering questions at the same time. This is a role for a product lawyer who is fluent in security and wants to sit at that intersection.

Your center of gravity is product counseling and security. Like everyone on this team, you'll also flex onto other work where you're needed.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Serve as the legal partner to Product and Engineering throughout the product lifecycle. You will join planning and design reviews, spot legal risk in new features and architecture changes (data flows, access controls, model and agent capabilities), and give real-time, practical guidance teams can act on

 - Draft and maintain product-facing terms and policies, including security terms, documentation disclosures, and the shared-responsibility model, and keep them consistent with how the product actually works

 - Serve as legal lead on security incidents to establish privilege, counsel Security and forensic partners, assess customer, contractual, and regulatory notification obligations, draft customer and regulator communications, and run post-incident reviews that turn lessons into controls

 - Own Baseten's security positions in customer paper (security addenda, exhibits, incident-notification, vulnerability-remediation, penetration-testing, and audit-rights), partner with Commercial on negotiating them, and align with Security and GRC on what we can and cannot commit to

 - Partner with Security and GRC on customer assurance including security questionnaires, customer and auditor reviews, Trust Center content, and the accuracy of security claims in sales and marketing materials

 - Partner with Capacity and Security on security and resilience across the compute supply chain including security and incident flow-downs to compute providers and colocation partners, supply-chain and third-party risk, and the export-control touchpoints owned by AI, Privacy & Governance

 - Support the certifications and controls program (SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, 27701, 42001, HIPAA-eligible configurations) with Security and Compliance, and advise on risk-acceptance decisions

 - Build playbooks, templates, incident runbooks, and tabletop exercises, and train Product, Engineering, and Security so that standard questions self-serve and novel ones reach Legal early

 - Stay current on AI, security, and privacy developments (EU AI Act, NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, DORA, U.S. state laws, and emerging AI-security guidance) and translate them into product requirements and recommended changes to our positions

 - Pitch in on customer and partnership deals, M&A, and other strategic or one-off work as needed, and help us scale the team

REQUIREMENTS

 - JD and active bar membership in good standing

 - 7+ years of legal experience, including in-house product counseling at an AI-native, B2B SaaS, cloud, or developer-infrastructure company

 - Demonstrated product-counsel instinct. You've advised a technical product or engineering org through the development lifecycle, not just papered deals, and can hold your own in a conversation about how the product works

 - Meaningful security experience in at least one of: security incident response and breach notification, negotiating security terms in enterprise agreements, or security and assurance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST CSF / SP 800-53, FedRAMP)

 - Working knowledge of privacy regimes (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA) as they surface in product design and security commitments

 - Technical fluency. Comfortable discussing APIs, cloud and multi-cloud architecture, data flows, encryption, and how models are deployed and served, and able to ask precise questions when you don't know

 - Calm under pressure with incomplete facts; sound judgment about when to act, when to seek a specialist, and when to escalate

 - Clear, direct communicator who can translate legal and technical concepts for engineers, customers, and executives, and push back constructively without slowing the team down

 - Thrives with autonomy on a lean, fast-moving team; knows when to own and when to escalate

NICE TO HAVE

 - The ability to learn, build, and master AI tooling and systems to self-serve and operate at breakneck speed, and an interest in building the framework for how Legal uses AI workflows to streamline its work

 - Experience at an AI, ML, GPU cloud, or developer-infrastructure company

 - Experience supporting regulated customers (healthcare, life sciences, financial services) on their security and resilience requirements

 - Hands-on experience with coordinated vulnerability disclosure, bug bounty programs, penetration testing, or SBOM practices

 - Experience with public-company cybersecurity governance and disclosure

 - Relevant certifications (CIPP/US, CIPP/E, CISSP, CISM, IAPP AIGP, or comparable)



BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

 - Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

 - Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.

Apply now to embark on a rewarding journey in shaping the future of AI! If you are a motivated individual with a passion for machine learning and a desire to be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking team, we would love to hear from you.

We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, or veteran status.

jobs.title: Integration & Test Engineer II
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Integration & Test Engineer II to help advance the development, testing, and production of Kaleidos, our portable, helium-cooled nuclear microreactor. With our first reactor built and production design underway, you'll work alongside a multidisciplinary team developing and executing tests that validate the performance, reliability, and safety of critical reactor hardware and systems.

Depending on your technical background and program needs, your work could span fluid systems, thermal management, mechanical assemblies, mechanisms, instrumentation, controls, and integrated reactor testing. You'll have opportunities to develop test procedures, build and operate test setups, troubleshoot hardware, analyze experimental data, and support engineering decisions through hands-on testing. This is an opportunity to contribute directly to the development and validation of Kaleidos as we advance toward commercial deployment.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Support development, qualification, and acceptance testing of reactor components, subsystems, and integrated hardware.

 - Develop and execute test plans and procedures to evaluate engineering requirements, hardware performance, and system reliability.

 - Assemble and operate test setups, including mechanical hardware, fluid systems, instrumentation, and data acquisition equipment.

 - Conduct test operations, monitor system behavior, and troubleshoot unexpected results or hardware issues.

 - Collaborate with mechanical, thermal, fluid systems, electrical, and controls engineers to develop test methods and resolve technical challenges.

 - Collect and analyze experimental data, compare results with engineering predictions, and support root cause investigations.

 - Identify test hazards, follow safety procedures, and support test readiness and risk mitigation activities.

 - Document test results, maintain test procedures, and recommend improvements to hardware, test methods, and processes.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, electrical engineering, or a related field from an accredited institution.

 - 2+ years of professional experience in engineering, hardware testing, systems integration, or test operations.

 - Strong engineering fundamentals in at least one area such as fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, mechanical systems, or electrical systems.

 - Experience developing or executing engineering tests, experimental methods, or hardware validation activities.

 - Experience with test instrumentation, data acquisition, troubleshooting, or engineering data analysis.

 - Ability to document technical work, solve engineering problems, and communicate findings across engineering disciplines.


DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience testing hardware in aerospace, nuclear, energy, automotive, or other high-reliability industries.

 - Hands-on experience with test stands, mechanical assemblies, fluid systems, instrumentation, or automated test equipment.

 - Familiarity with pressure systems, thermal testing, mechanical testing, or electromechanical systems.

 - Experience with sensors, data acquisition systems, PLCs, or engineering tools such as Python, MATLAB, or LabVIEW.

 - Experience interpreting engineering drawings, P&IDs, test procedures, or technical specifications.

 - Experience with hardware integration, commissioning, troubleshooting, or production acceptance testing.


ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

 - Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as necessary to accomplish our mission.

 - Must work 100% onsite at El Segundo HQ.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Nuclear Engineering Certificate Program: 100% covered educational program with Penn State University, for eligible employees, to rapidly upscale into nuclear.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s full-time new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.
