jobs.title: Lead Physical Security Hardware Specialist (East Coast & International)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

LEAD PHYSICAL SECURITY HARDWARE SPECIALIST (EAST COAST & INTERNATIONAL)

Help SpaceX protect life and property anywhere company assets are deployed by leading a team of Security Hardware Specialists and Senior Security Hardware Specialists. The Lead Physical Security Hardware Specialist is responsible for delivering and maintaining the physical security technology that protects SpaceX personnel, facilities, and assets, including access control systems (ACS), closed-circuit television (CCTV)/video management systems (VMS), intrusion detection systems (IDS), and related platforms. Reporting to the enterprise leader for Security Systems and Technology, this role typically oversees multiple facilities across a region. This is a people-management role requiring strong technical judgment, project management skills, and experience leading geographically distributed teams while managing a large portfolio of concurrent projects. The Lead translates department priorities into execution, develops team members, and ensures installations, upgrades, maintenance, repairs, and programming are completed safely and reliably. As the organization grows, this role also owns assigned enterprise programs and is accountable for important aspects of physical security technology operations across SpaceX.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Lead physical security hardware operations for an assigned region or a large, complex site, balancing project delivery, preventive maintenance, service requests, and urgent operational needs

• Directly manage, mentor, and develop Physical Security Hardware Specialists and Senior Physical Security Hardware Specialists, including setting expectations, giving regular feedback, managing performance, supporting career progression, and leading hiring and onboarding for your area

• Manage a large portfolio of concurrent physical security technology projects from initial assessment and planning through installation, commissioning, acceptance, and transition to ongoing support

• Define project scope, schedules, milestones, resource requirements, and success criteria; track dependencies, risks, changes, and costs; and take corrective action when delivery is at risk

• Allocate personnel and coordinate coverage across facilities, matching assignments to technical capabilities, business priorities, and site requirements

• Own assigned enterprise programs, such as preventive maintenance planning, hardware lifecycle management, audit, or technical training; establish program plans, procedures, metrics, and reporting, and coordinate execution across the enterprise

• Use JIRA or a comparable ticketing and project tracking system to prioritize work, assign ownership, monitor backlogs, and maintain visibility into service requests, project status, and completion

• Provide technical oversight for access control systems, CCTV/video management systems, intrusion detection systems, and related physical security infrastructure; guide complex troubleshooting and engage system administrators or other specialist as needed

• Oversee site assessments, job walks, installation planning, testing, and commissioning to ensure work meets operational needs and established enterprise standards

• Coordinate with Physical Security, Facilities, IT, Information Security, Purchasing, system administrators, and other stakeholders to resolve dependencies and deliver integrated security capabilities

• Manage vendor and contractor execution within assigned projects, including scope coordination, scheduling, installation quality, deliverables, and issue resolution

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certification

• 5+ years of experience managing enterprise-level physical security systems such as CCTV, access control, VMS, intrusion detection systems, fire and alarm systems), or alert systems

• 1+ years of direct leadership responsibility across global sites

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience leading physical security hardware teams supporting complex facilities, large campuses, or regional operations

• Experience owning a program across multiple sites or business units, including developing procedures, establishing performance measures, and driving consistent execution

• Subject matter expert in Genetec Security Center, with experience in Lenel access control and/or Avigilon systems, and relevant manufacturer certifications

• Strong project planning and portfolio management skills, with experience coordinating internal teams, vendors, and contractors across competing priorities

• Experience using JIRA, Confluence, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Monday.com, or comparable project tracking and documentation tools

• Ability to interpret system drawings, installation plans, wiring diagrams, and technical specifications, and to evaluate installation quality and readiness for acceptance

• Experience with preventive maintenance programs, hardware lifecycle planning, inventory management, and recurring issue resolution

• Experience preparing project estimates, tracking budgets, and evaluating vendor proposals

• Experience in space exploration, aviation, military, manufacturing, or another high-risk, high-reliability operating environment

• Strong communication, decision-making, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to explain technical issues and delivery risks clearly

• Demonstrated ability to develop technical talent, establish accountability, and keep execution on track in a fast-paced environment with changing prioriti

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be willing to work all shifts, extended hours, and/or weekends as needed

• Willingness to travel as needed (up to 35% or more)

• Ability to work in active construction, industrial, and outdoor environments while following applicable safety requirements

• Must be able to obtain a TS/SCI clearance

• An active clearance may provide the opportunity for you to work on sensitive SpaceX missions; if so, you will be subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol testing

• Position is subject to random drug and alcohol testing

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

MECHANICAL ENGINEERING MANAGER, FLUIDS SYSTEMS

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Lead the mechanical engineering team that designs, builds, commissions, and sustains data center cooling and fluid systems, including chilled water and condenser water plants, CDUs, rear-door and in-row heat exchangers, liquid-to-chip or cold-plate loops where used, piping, pumps, valves, and heat rejection.

• Own the heat-rejection architecture from IT load to the ambient sink, including redundancy, failure modes, and ride-through, and hold the plant accountable for temperature, flow, and available IT capacity.

• Set technical direction and approve critical work: P&IDs, hydraulic and thermal calculations, equipment specifications, construction details, and commissioning procedures.

• Drive design of flow, pressure drop, pump and valve selection, NPSH, water hammer, expansion, water chemistry, filtration, materials compatibility, and leak detection. Require calculations, not vendor defaults.

• Partner with electrical, controls, IT infrastructure, construction, and operations so mechanical design matches power, BMS/EPMS, whitespace layout, and how the site is run.

• Own capacity planning with operations: current supportable IT load, the first constraint, and what must be built before the next deployment.

• Run design reviews, change control, and root-cause on thermal or fluid incidents. Close issues with hardware or procedure changes.

• Hire, develop, and direct mechanical engineers. Set clear ownership, give direct feedback, and raise the bar on analysis and field judgment.

• Manage schedule, cost, and vendor performance for cooling and fluid scope without giving up technical control.

• Treat safety, pressure systems, water and chemical handling, and construction interfaces as non-negotiable.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or another engineering discipline.

• 5+ years of mechanical engineering experience on industrial fluid, HVAC, or process cooling systems, such as data centers, high-performance computing, power generation, semiconductor facilities, or similar mission-critical plants.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES:

• Experience leading engineers or serving as the responsible engineer for chilled water, condenser water, or liquid cooling systems, including pumps, piping, heat exchangers, cooling towers or dry coolers, and controls integration.

• Demonstrated ability to review a P&ID and pump curve, perform a heat and flow balance, and identify where a design fails under normal and partial-failure conditions.

• Experience taking hardware through construction and commissioning, including punch list, test and balance, functional testing, and turnover to operations

• Direct data center experience on air-side, liquid-side, or both, including high-density or direct liquid cooling.

• Working knowledge of ASME B31.x piping, ASHRAE data center guidance, relevant NFPA requirements, and local mechanical codes as applied to these plants.

• Experience with water treatment, materials compatibility, and corrosion control on open and closed loops.

• Experience adding new cooling capacity, not only maintaining an existing plant.

• Experience coordinating mechanical scope with electrical distribution and a building or plant control system.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be able to work onsite at Starbase, TX.

• Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jobs.description:
Company Overview 

Promise modernizes how government agencies and utilities support people in financial difficulty. We build technology that makes it simple for residents to receive benefits, engage with assistance programs, set up flexible payment plans, and stay on track—while helping agencies increase efficiency, recover revenue, and deliver services with dignity. Our mission is to transform public systems so they work better for everyone, especially the most vulnerable.



Our team includes experts from companies like Palantir, Google, Stripe , and esteemed government leaders. We work hard and believe deeply in what we do. We're looking for excellent people to build innovative, resilient technology.



Backed by over $50 million in funding from top investors – such as Reid Hoffman, Howard Schultz, Michael Seibel, Y Combinator, 8VC, The General Partnership, First Round Capital, Kapor Capital, XYZ Ventures, and Bronze Investments – Promise has been recognized as one of Fast Company's "World's Most Innovative Companies of 2022,” “Forbes Next Billion-Dollar Startups 2024,” and Y Combinator’s #1 GovTech startup.


ABOUT THE ROLE

You will be the person who knows what is actually happening with our accounts: where adoption is strong, where it is stalling, where the political winds are shifting, and where there is room to expand and upsell.

You will work directly with senior stakeholders inside utility companies, and municipal agencies, alongside our internal Product, Sales, Outreach, and Implementation teams. Your job is to make sure our customers get real value from Promise, and to make sure Promise never misses a signal that could turn into churn risk or expansion opportunity.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the relationship. Be the primary point of contact for a portfolio of large accounts, focusing specifically on those accounts utilizing Promise’s PromisePay services. Know the people, the politics, and the pressures inside each agency better than anyone else at Promise. Directly manage requests from our clients, efficiently providing responses and solutions to their inquiries - no question or request is too big or too small for you to manage.

 - Drive adoption. Monitor usage and engagement across your accounts. Identify where adoption is lagging and build the plan to fix it before it becomes a renewal problem.

 - Spot and drive expansion. Flag opportunities where an account is ready for a larger footprint and more Promise services, whether that's more programs, more departments, or a broader contract. Build the business case and hand it to Sales to close, then stay in the room as the customer's advocate.

 - Manage the handoff, both ways. Take over account relationships from the Sales team as implementation happens and stabilizes. When an account expands into new commercial territory, new pricing, or a new deployment, partner with the Implementation team  for that phase and pick it back up once things are live again.

 - Close the loop with Product. Collect and prioritize product feedback from customers and route it back to the Product team with context, not just a list of complaints. Help Product understand why something matters to a customer and what problem it would solve, not just what the feature request was.

 - Manage renewal risk. Proactively track account health and get ahead of risk signals. If something is not working, say so internally, early, and clearly. Recruit help so that we can intervene and fix things.

 - Represent Promise in the room. Run regular business reviews with customer stakeholders. Come prepared. Never walk in cold. Take notes and report out with clear tasks and timelines.

 - Feed the institutional knowledge base. What you learn in the field belongs to the whole company. Document it and share it so the next person does not have to relearn it.




WHAT WILL HELP YOU SUCCEED

 - 3+ years in customer success, account management, or delivery roles serving enterprise or public sector customers — utilities, state or municipal agencies, health and human services, or similarly regulated buyers. You have owned relationships where the customer could not simply churn quietly, and where a bad quarter shows up in a public meeting.

 - Strategic and Proactive Hands-on Approach. You develop strong relationships. You spot trends and issues before the client does and take action, as needed, to remedy them. You know the difference between a customer who is actively using the product/service vs. one that hasn’t fully embraced the solution and you know how to move them towards fully embracing our products and services. You are known as the best customer success representative that they work with.

 - You track the context of the client. You can read where a decision really sits and who has to say yes before anything moves. You staff the utility decision maker appropriately, helping them move to contact renewals and upsells. You understand what is important to them and you put that information in front of them.

 - Experience owning account health outcomes — renewal risk, adoption, or expansion — for a portfolio of large, complex customers.

 - You use data to make an argument, not to fill a slide. You can pull adoption and throughput numbers, figure out what is actually driving them, and turn that into a specific plan with a named owner and a date.

 - Willingness to travel up to 20–30% to be on site with customers. Some of the most important conversations in this role happen in-person.




WHO THRIVES AT PROMISE

You’ll love it here if:

 - You are energized by big, complex challenges and the opportunity to solve them.

 - You want your work to have a real, measurable impact on people’s lives.

 - You take ownership and run toward problems, not away from them.

 - You value clear, candid, and constructive communication.

Promise is not for you if:

 - You prefer hierarchy and rigid structures. We operate with freedom and responsibility.

 - You are uncomfortable with change. We move fast, adapt often, and expect agility.

 - You want a typical corporate culture. We are mission-driven, ambitious, and direct.

 - You believe efficiency means “doing less.” We believe efficiency means doing better.

 

How We Enable Our People

 - 100% paid health coverage

 - Flexible time off (take what you need) and sick leave

 - Lunch, snacks, and coffee provided in office

 - Company retreats

 - Hybrid work: we deeply value in-person collaboration and are in-office or onsite at least 4 days a week

jobs.title: Senior Nuclear Engineer, Safety Analysis
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Senior Nuclear Engineer, Safety Analysis to help advance the development, testing, and production of Kaleidos, our portable, helium-cooled nuclear microreactor. With our first reactor built and production design underway, you'll work alongside a multidisciplinary team evaluating reactor safety, performance, and behavior under normal, transient, and accident conditions.

Your work will span reactor systems modeling, thermal hydraulics, accident analysis, fuel performance, source term development, and radiological consequence assessments. You'll take ownership of complex safety analyses, evaluate reactor behavior and safety margins, validate computational models, and help shape engineering decisions that support the safe design and commercial deployment of Kaleidos.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own complex reactor safety analyses and evaluations that directly inform reactor design, safety margins, testing, and regulatory decisions.

 - Develop and apply engineering models to evaluate reactor behavior during normal operation, transients, and postulated accident scenarios.

 - Perform safety evaluations involving thermal hydraulics, fuel performance, source terms, radiological consequences, or other relevant areas.

 - Evaluate modeling assumptions, uncertainties, sensitivities, and conservatism to establish technically defensible safety conclusions.

 - Collaborate with nuclear, mechanical, thermal, materials, and controls engineers to evaluate design alternatives and resolve safety-related technical challenges.

 - Support reactor testing by establishing validation requirements, evaluating experimental data, and correlating analytical predictions with test results.

 - Develop, validate, and improve safety analysis tools and methods, including Radiant's Digital Twin, through benchmarking and verification and validation.

jobs.title: Director, Consulting
jobs.description:
NAC International, a global provider of nuclear fuel cycle management solutions and consulting services, is seeking an accomplished, client-focused Director, Consulting to help lead, deliver and grow our Consulting business unit. The Director, Consulting reports to the Vice President, Consulting.

About the Business

NAC International is a dynamic and forward-thinking leader in the global nuclear industry. As pioneers in nuclear fuel cycle technology and waste management solutions for over 50 years, we are dedicated to advancing the safe and sustainable use of nuclear energy.

NAC’s Consulting business delivers dependable, highly specialized insights to nuclear utilities, suppliers, governments, agencies, and the investment and financial communities, including nuclear fuel market analysis and price forecasts, fuel procurement strategy, fuel and core component performance and fabrication oversight, nuclear quality assurance, nuclear material control and accountability, and government policy support.

Our consulting services are supported by an internationally recognized network of industry experts and by NAC's exclusive data-driven market research, including Fuel-Trac® and our flagship Nuclear Fuel Market Issues & Insights report. With renewed global demand for nuclear energy, NAC is seeking a seasoned leader to help sustain the company's ongoing success and growth.

About the Position

As the Director, Consulting, you will work alongside the Vice President, Consulting to lead all aspects of the Consulting business unit, from strategy and business development to project execution, client relationships and the management of our global network of consultants. You will bring a deep, practical understanding of the commercial nuclear power industry and the nuclear fuel supply chain, gained from hands-on experience in the utility, supplier or related sectors, and you will help extend NAC's services to the growing new nuclear market, including nuclear newcomer countries, new reactor developers and new fuel cycle facilities. You will be responsible for driving revenue and profit growth while aligning with corporate goals, policies, and strategies, ensuring the delivery of high-quality consulting services, and pursuing new business opportunities, including serving as an initial point of contact for clients seeking technical solutions from NAC's other business units. Your leadership will be key in sustaining NAC International's reputation for independence, excellence and innovation.

Key Responsibilities

• Partner with the Vice President, Consulting to develop and execute business area plans and strategies for the Consulting business unit, ensuring alignment with corporate objectives, and act on the Vice President's behalf as needed.

• Share responsibility for the business unit's financial performance, including revenue and profit targets, budgets, forecasts, pricing and resource planning.

• Pursue and develop new domestic and international business opportunities with nuclear utilities, fuel cycle suppliers, intermediaries, reactor vendors, and governments/agencies.

• Lead the preparation of compelling, competitive proposals, and negotiate consulting agreements, scopes of work and pricing with clients.

• Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with commercial and government clients, key account personnel, and industry stakeholders, ensuring customer satisfaction and loyalty.

• Seek opportunities to expand tasking and grow revenues under longstanding client relationships and contracts, including those with the DOE.

• Lead consulting projects to ensure compliance with contract commitments including deliverable document content and schedule requirements.

• Contribute to and oversee NAC's market intelligence products and services, including the Fuel-Trac® system, the annual Nuclear Fuel Market Issues & Insights report, and the growing suite of nuclear fuel cycle training seminars.

• Lead the growth of NAC's consulting services for the new nuclear market, including feasibility studies and roadmaps for nuclear newcomer countries, regulatory framework development (regulations, regulatory guides and license application review procedures), and fuel procurement & contracting.

• Grow the client base for NAC Reporter®, NAC's state- and facility-level nuclear material accounting and control (MC&A) software suite.

• Oversee spent fuel and radioactive waste management consulting, including interim storage and permanent disposal options analyses, storage and transport procurement support, transport container licensing support, reprocessing and recycling economics, and disposal program support such as disposal regulations, site evaluation, waste acceptance criteria, safety cases and deep geologic repository concepts.

• Expand, manage and mentor a high-performance network of employees and contract consultants that meet the company's needs and contract requirements, fostering a culture of teamwork, continuous improvement and professional development.

• Represent NAC at industry conferences, fuel market forums and professional organizations, delivering presentations and strengthening NAC's position as a trusted, independent voice in the nuclear fuel market.

• Monitor trends in nuclear fuel markets, plant operations and fleet strategies (such as power uprates, longer fuel cycles, license renewals and new nuclear deployment) to identify new consulting opportunities and develop new products and services.

• Pursue consulting opportunities to serve as a bridge for technical solution offerings from NAC's other business units (spent fuel storage and transportation systems, NAC Philotechnics D&D, radioactive waste and health physics services, and Niagara Energy Products nuclear-grade fabrication and precision machining).

• Play an active role in NAC’s Spent Fuel Academy and Nuclear Fuel Cycle Seminar, including serving as an instructor and contributing to program content and delivery.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Nuclear Engineering, or in another engineering or physical science discipline closely related to nuclear power.

• Fifteen (15) years of progressive experience in the commercial nuclear power industry, including a minimum of five (5) years in nuclear fuel procurement, fuel supply management, nuclear fuel engineering or core design.

• A minimum of five (5) years of management or supervisory experience leading technical or operational teams.

• Demonstrated experience developing and executing nuclear fuel procurement strategies, and negotiating and administering contracts with suppliers or clients for nuclear fuel materials, services or related products.

• A deep understanding of the nuclear fuel cycle and nuclear fuel markets, including uranium, conversion, enrichment and fuel fabrication, and of how fuel supply decisions affect plant operations and economics.

• An established reputation and a broad network of contacts across nuclear utilities, fuel cycle suppliers and industry organizations.

• Demonstrated ability to comfortably engage clients and stakeholders at all levels of the organizational hierarchy, including top company executives and senior government officials.

• Excellent presentation, organization, analytical and writing skills, including an ability to effectively communicate complex technical and commercial information.

• Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally, as required, to successfully grow the Consulting business unit.

Preferred Qualifications

• Registered Professional Engineer (P.E.)

• Project Management Professional (PMP) certification

• Experience managing nuclear fuel supply for a multi-unit utility fleet, including long-term fuel planning, inventory management and supply diversification.

• Leadership roles in nuclear fuel market or industry organizations (for example, World Nuclear Fuel Market, American Nuclear Society, Nuclear Energy Institute or World Nuclear Association).

• Operating plant experience in reactor engineering, operations, outage management, work management or major plant modification projects such as power uprates; a current or former NRC Senior Reactor Operator (SRO) license or certification is a plus.

• Working knowledge of NRC licensing and regulatory requirements as they relate to nuclear fuel and plant operations.

• Business development, consulting or client-facing commercial experience, including success winning competitive proposals.

• A proven record of leading organizational change and performance improvement, and of developing and mentoring staff.

Benefits

At NAC, we are committed to providing competitive pay and benefits that are in line with industry standards. NAC offers Company paid health insurance, long and short disability and life insurance, generous paid time off benefits, 11 paid holidays, 401k with employer matching contributions, tuition reimbursement, and remote hybrid work.

NAC is an Equal Opportunity Employer and strives for diversity. In accordance with applicable law, NAC does not discriminate in hiring or otherwise in employment based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, marital or veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Car Owners: 25-Minute Survey on Automotive Ownership Experiences

WHAT WE'RE RESEARCHING

We're running a paid study on automotive ownership and the day-to-day realities of maintaining a luxury personal vehicle. Your feedback helps us understand shifting consumer preferences and pain points in the modern automotive market.


HOW IT WORKS

You will complete a 25-minute remote survey from your computer or smartphone. The session includes a mix of standard multiple-choice questions and prompts requiring spoken answers. You will reflect on your personal vehicle history, ownership satisfaction, and future preferences. A working microphone is required to record your voice responses clearly.


WHO THIS IS FOR

We welcome current luxury car owners who are comfortable recording their thoughts out loud. We are looking for drivers with a wide variety of vehicle types, brands, and ownership histories. Both primary drivers and shared household vehicle owners are encouraged to apply.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Complete a 25-minute remote survey regarding your vehicle ownership

 - Answer multiple-choice questions about your driving habits and preferences

 - Record clear voice responses to specific prompts using your device's microphone


WHO SHOULD APPLY

 - Current or recent automotive owner

jobs.title: Sr Research Associate
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

The Senior Research Associate performs research and/or development tasks in collaboration with others.  Makes detailed observations, analyzes data, and interprets results.  Investigates creates and develops new methods and technologies for project advancement.  Maintains a high level of professional expertise through familiarity with scientific literature.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Design, plan, and perform experiments geared towards the development of non-invasive prenatal tests and cancer detection tests.

• Autonomously and accurately plan and execute complex laboratory experiments Analyze data using advanced analytical tools

• Keep a detailed laboratory notebook; write protocols and experimental plans, and document results and scientific interpretations

• Contribute insight toward experimental findings and troubleshoot laboratory processes and protocols

• Communicate and discuss results with a multidisciplinary team including biologists, bioinformaticians, statisticians, software engineers, and managers

• Summarize work in research reports and laboratory meeting presentations

• Learn and understand the science behind ongoing research projects while simultaneously completing increasingly complex tasks.

• This role will have occasional access to PHI both in paper and electronic form and have occasional access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job.

• The employee must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire.

• Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements.

QUALIFICATIONS:

• B.S. degree in molecular biology, related field, or equivalent.

• Minimum of 3 - 4 years of industry experience in an assay development department.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

• Extensive hands-on experience with nucleic acid techniques, including DNA manipulation, PCR, qPCR, DNA quantification, and analysis using LabChip and BioAnalyzer.

• Experience with Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) techniques and protocols.

• Knowledge and experience in target enrichment, cfDNA/RNA, and NGS data analysis.

• Automation skill set is a must, including experience with developing or executing assays on automated liquid handling platforms.

• Exceptional communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• Demonstrated success in both collaborative and individual projects.

• Proficiency in data analysis using Excel or similar software; working knowledge of R or JMP is a plus.

• Experience with reagent quality control (QC) is a plus.

• Self-driven and strong team player with proven track record

Compensation & Total Rewards

This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of  hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and skills considerations.

This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including:

• Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)

• 401(k) with company match

• Generous paid time off and company holidays

• Additional wellness and work-life benefits

Compensation Range

$108,600—$135,700 USD

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program!

jobs.title: Global Supply Manager (Power Generation)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

GLOBAL SUPPLY MANAGER (POWER GENERATION)

The SpaceX supply chain department is a critical player in enabling SpaceX mission. To capitalize on SpaceX’s technological and market changing successes, our team will be part of managing an agile yet robust supply chain that will enable a competitive advantage for the company. The functions within the department include procurement, planning and fulfillment, supplier development and quality, logistics and inventory. SpaceX supply chain will play a key role in enabling SpaceX to meet the ambitious growth targets and greatly contribute in making us a multi-planetary species. This individual will support fuel & gas supply, capital purchases and projects for the production, test and launch organizations, including power-generation and electrical capital equipment for large facilities.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Create sourcing strategies for assigned categories to reduce risk and meet targets for the purchasing department including, but not limited to, payment terms, cash targets, and cost savings

• Develop and maintain key internal stakeholder relationships to create strategic sourcing models that optimize the value of products and services that support business unit requirements to maintain continuous cost reduction programs for controllable expenditures

• Present confidently to decision makers on launch critical response events

• Communicate, manage, and drive compliance to category strategies

• Collaborate with stakeholders to define Service Level Agreements and KPIs for suppliers and measure the appropriate criteria, such as: delivery of business results, cost reduction, quality and timeliness of delivery

• Conduct research, perform benchmarking, and gather market analysis for assigned categories

• Source power-generation and electrical capital equipment, including generators, gas turbines, switchgear, transformers, UPS systems, and related balance-of-plant infrastructure, through RFP/RFQ, total cost of ownership, and competitive bidding on multi-million-dollar CAPEX purchases

• Create contract documents in collaboration with the legal department

• Manage contracts to ensure the performance of the supplier to contract obligations

• Understand interrelationships between contracts and terms while applying creativity and sound business reasoning to interpret application of contract to business needs

• Maximize value and cost savings benefits while lowering risk through strategic negotiations

• Identify and drive year over year cost optimization through reducing usage and eliminating waste within our operations

• Establish preferred suppliers for assigned categories

• Create and implement management programs to develop, continuously improve, manage the performance of, and monitor KPIs of the supply base

• Place purchase orders and resolve blocked invoices related to assigned categories

• Develop and lead efforts to reduce number of transactions and for assigned categories

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Advanced degree and 4+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or bachelor’s degree and 6+ years of experience working in one or more of the following; or 10+ years of experience working in one or more of the following: Engineering Purchasing Contract negotiation Material or production planning Operations or supply chain management Material cost control

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience procuring generators, switchgear, transformers, UPS systems, and related electrical balance-of-plant for large facilities, ideally in energy, industrial, or heavy-manufacturing environments

• Working knowledge of the gas turbine OEM landscape, long-lead capital equipment, spare parts / aftermarket, and service agreements (LTSA, O&M, overhaul, field service)

• Understanding of gas turbine and SCR technical drivers (output, heat rate, availability, NOx/CO performance, catalyst life, reagent consumption) and how they affect total cost of ownership

• Experience with capital project procurement: RFPs, bid evaluation, T&Cs, FAT/SAT, commissioning support, and coordination with engineering, facilities, test, and launch stakeholders

• Strong background in total cost of ownership (TCO) analysis, supply risk mitigation, dual-sourcing strategies, and ensuring continuity of supply for critical manufacturing or production operations

• Demonstrated success implementing supplier performance scorecards, quality/compliance programs, and logistics optimization (lead-time management, inventory, safety stock for turbine and SCR products) while driving cost savings and service level improvements

• Experience negotiating complex commercial agreements (pricing, escalation, liquidated damages, warranties, IP, export control, and long-term supply) with OEMs, fabricators, and specialty suppliers

• Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, specifications, P&IDs, and quality documentation to align sourcing with engineering intent

• Experience with technical procurement, manufacturing, or designing production components

• Knowledge of relevant codes, quality systems, and compliance (ASME, API, ISO, environmental/air-permit constraints, ITAR/EAR as applicable)

• Ability to prove a strong track record of leadership and team building

• Remarkable problem-solving skills with a bias for speed and positive impact

• Ability to learn quickly and prioritize appropriately to meet customer and company needs

• Exceptional analytical and organizational skills

• Excellent customer service skills, produce exceptional work at all times, highly self-motivated

• Effective written, verbal and presentation communication skills

• Strong technical knowledge and skills in current technologies and applications (e.g. MS Office Suite, SQL, PowerBI, etc.)

• Detail-oriented, and able to respond quickly to a fast-moving and ever-changing environment

• Holds self to highest ethical standards, and conducts all activities with the highest of integrity

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

As a full-time team member, you will have access to the following benefits:

• Paid Time Off – 15 days accrued in year 1, 9 holidays, and 1 day of Volunteering Time Off

• 401k (eligible upon completion of 90 days of employment and must be at least 18 years of age)

Purpose of the Position:

The Director of Career Services provides strategic leadership and oversight for graduate placement initiatives, ensuring alignment with institutional goals and industry demands. This role drives performance across the Career Services team, fosters cross-functional collaboration with Corporate Alliance and Graduate Success teams, and supports business development efforts to enhance employment outcomes and partnerships.

• Team Member Engagement and Opportunity Creation: Establish and maintain systems to identify employment opportunities, while cultivating relationships with employers to expand graduate job prospects.

• Graduate Support and Career Readiness: Provide career coaching and job readiness support to graduates, including interview preparation and guidance for securing employment in their field of study.

• Compliance and Institutional Alignment: Ensure departmental compliance with regulatory and accreditation standards, while contributing to cross-departmental initiatives and institutional goals.

• Lead with Care: Lead, coach, and develop team members, fostering a culture of wellness, recognition, and engagement. Meet regularly with direct reports in one-on-one and group settings to provide feedback and cultivate/maintain a positive work culture.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

Career Level Expectations:

• Typically manages multiple teams or a department.

• Requires a high degree of responsibility for resources and frequently influences business decisions made by functional leadership.

• Owns short to mid-term (1-3 years) strategy, execution and operational direction for multiple departments which directly impacts the achievement of overall functional results.

• Problems faced are frequently complex and require extensive investigation and analysis in collaboration with others.

• Requires the ability to influence others to accept practices and approaches, and ability to communicate with executive leadership.

• Desire for growth and professional development.

Required Skills/Experience:

• Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 5 years of experience in recruiting, career services and employment assistance, or in sales.

• Ability to professionally communicate fluently in verbal and written English.

• Ability to contribute to a diverse and inclusive work environment.

• Computer literacy/basic computer skills to effectively navigate and utilize the technology required for the role.

Preferred Requirements:

• Director level experience.

• Strong analytical skill set.

• Proficient in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and other business tools such as Microsoft Teams.

Compliance:

• Demonstrate knowledge of and carefully follow all applicable federal and state compliance requirements and regulations including those prescribed by the U.S. Department of Education, accrediting agencies, state regulations, and internal policies and procedures.

• Effectively communicate compliance requirements to other staff as appropriate and quickly escalate any compliance concerns to the Compliance department.

Work Environment/Physical Demands:

• This is a remote position.

• Home office set up, quiet place to work, and ability to hard wire into high-speed internet connection.

• May require setup of computer equipment; accommodation consideration available upon request.

• Flexibility to work evenings and weekends, as needed.

In addition to the compensation listed below, this position includes a cell phone allowance and eligibility for an annual incentive bonus.

Compensation Range

$100,000—$100,000 USD

OUR VALUES

Our institutional values are shaped and validated by our team members. They describe how we strive to operate and are the standards of behavior we look to embody.

ACT WITH INTEGRITY

We operate honestly and ethically in an industry-compliant fashion. We are fair and trustworthy in our interactions with all we serve. Our team members, at all levels, lead by example and strive to do the right thing for our students and for each other. We are disciplined professionals who strive to be straightforward and dependable.

CHAMPION STUDENT OUTCOMES

We live by a strong commitment to our students and are passionate about preparing them for meaningful careers. We are deeply dedicated to ensuring students’ educational and career success. We excel at building our students’ confidence and empowering them to reach their full potential.

COMMIT TO TEAM MEMBER SUCCESS

We are committed to our team members’ success and to each other’s success. We strive to create an environment that attracts and retains the best talent while offering continuous learning, professional development and career growth opportunities. We recognize and reward our team members for their contributions to the organization and to our students.

PURSUE RESULTS WITH PURPOSE

We pursue results with a sense of urgency and purpose. We take responsibility for achieving ambitious, measurable results and hold each other accountable. We think strategically and critically, greet new ideas and challenges openly, and look for innovative solutions to challenges.

HAVE FUN. BUILD ENERGY

Enjoying what we do is central to achieving our goals. Building energy, having fun, being optimistic and creating a positive working environment are all critical to our success and that of our students. We strive to be inspired and to inspire others. We consistently show appreciation and celebrate our successes, both large and small.

WORK AS ONE

We believe that diverse, inclusive teams produce breakthrough results. We strive to build and maintain positive relationships with colleagues from all types of backgrounds by showing respect and humility when interacting with each other and resolving conflicts in a constructive manner. By working together, we win together - as one - ensuring that the goals of the company are the focal point of our efforts.

jobs.title: Medical Malpractice & Nursing Home Litigation Attorney
jobs.location: Atlanta, Georgia, United States; Boston, Massachusetts, United States; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States
jobs.description:
At Morgan & Morgan, the work we do matters. For millions of Americans, we’re their last line of defense against insurance companies, large corporations or defective goods. From attorneys in all 50 states, to client support staff, creative marketing to operations teams, every member of our firm has a key role to play in the winning fight for consumer rights. Our over 6,000 employees are all united by one mission: For the People.

As part of the Medical Malpractice & Nursing Home Litigation team at Morgan & Morgan, you'll use your skills to advocate for some of the most vulnerable members of our communities—elderly residents and their families who have suffered neglect, abuse, preventable injuries, and devastating losses in nursing homes and long-term care facilities. These are not just cases. They are stories of broken trust, dignity compromised, and families searching for answers. They deserve an attorney who is equal parts advocate, strategist, and counselor. Someone who understands that behind every medical record, deposition, and motion is a person whose voice needs to be heard. If that resonates with you, we'd like to meet you.

The Opportunity

As a Medical Malpractice & Nursing Home Litigation Attorney at Morgan & Morgan, you will manage a substantial and meaningful caseload from intake through trial. You'll work alongside a nationally respected team with the resources, reputation, and support necessary to take on powerful opponents and achieve life-changing results for clients. Here, you'll have the autonomy to eventually lead your cases, the backing of a premier plaintiffs' firm, and the opportunity to build a career dedicated to making a genuine difference.

What You'll Do & Where You’ll Do It

• Handle medical malpractice, nursing home negligence / abuse, and wrongful death matters from pre-suit investigation through trial

• Leverage M&M’s technology suite to effectively manage cases through their lifecycle

• Build compelling cases through discovery, expert development, depositions, and motion practice

• Guide clients and families through some of the most difficult moments of their lives with compassion and clarity

jobs.title: Senior Robotics Algorithms and Controls Engineer
jobs.description:
The Advanced Product Development (APD) team leverages and advances the cutting-edge of technology to design and develop the surgical robotic systems of the future. Robotics Algorithms and Controls engineers (Systems Analysts) perform a central role in the design, development, and support of new products in the da Vinci product line. They are responsible for developing the surgical teleoperation, motion control, and safety algorithms. This responsibility crosses into electrical, mechanical, software, control, user interface, and safety engineering. Systems Analysts strive to provide early design input, prove out new designs, and seek out solutions to challenging problems.

As a Senior Systems Analyst you will work with a small, multidisciplinary team of talented and dedicated engineers. This position is the software-oriented track within Systems Analysis, bridging the team’s algorithms and the software infrastructure they run on. You will own the software layer between the application and the real-time control loop, the bring-up of the embedded compute platform, the software side of the FPGA interface, and you will bring enough fluency in control algorithms to connect their signals to the right system modes and safety responses. Systems Analysts maintain awareness and interest in developing research and technologies related to medical devices and safety-critical systems and actively apply this knowledge to system design.

Essential Job Duties

•       Design, implement, and own the software layer between the application software and the real-time control loop.

•       Bring up the embedded compute platform and real-time execution environment for new prototype systems.

•       Own the software interface to the FPGA, including drivers and data paths between processors and FPGA logic.

•       Integrate prototype hardware with existing systems and lead embedded bring-up of new manipulators, instruments, and controller boards.

•       Implement control and safety algorithms developed with Systems Analysts as deterministic, production-quality embedded software.

•       Design and implement servo control systems with Systems Analysts, applying control theory to mechatronic and tele-robotic platforms.

•       Connect algorithm signals to the appropriate system modes and safety responses in partnership with the Systems Analysts who own the supervisory logic.

•       Root-cause problems that cross the hardware, software, and control boundary.

•       Develop test, continuous integration, simulation, and hardware-in-the-loop infrastructure for Systems Analysis software; provide tool building for other engineering issues.

•       Document software design, risks, requirements, and test protocols; document and communicate intellectual property.

•       Participate in clinical observations and experiments to ensure that performance requirements are relevant and realistic.

•       Communicate system performance to the organization and support it as products evolve from design engineering to manufacturing.

•       Act as an interface between Systems Analysis and Software Engineering; take ownership of issues that cross disciplinary boundaries.

Required Skills and Experience

•       Strong embedded development skills, including intimate knowledge of C and modern C++, and experience with unit testing, continuous integration, and modern build systems.

•       Experience developing software under real-time constraints, with a solid understanding of determinism, latency, and execution-time analysis.

•       Experience with embedded architectures on multi-processor SoC/FPGA platforms, including bare-metal or RTOS development, device drivers, and inter-processor communication.

•       Hands-on experience bringing up embedded platforms and integrating prototype hardware with software.

•       Working knowledge of control systems and robotics sufficient to read, modify, and reason about control code and its timing.

•       MATLAB and Python programming capabilities for analysis, simulation, and tool building.

•       Comfort with the concepts of design input, design output, traceability, and risk analysis.

•       Detail-oriented, with the ability to develop and drive a single solution to completion.

•       Hands-on engineering experience with a proven ability to work well in a team environment.

•       Self-motivated and proactive in engaging with interdisciplinary teams to address and solve complex problems.

•       A desire to deliver a quality and innovative product that will improve millions of people’s lives.

Required Education and Training

•       Minimum MS degree in CS, EE, ME, or a similar field with 4–5+ years of industrial experience, or a PhD with 1–3+ years of experience, or a BS with 7+ years of relevant industrial experience.

Working Conditions

•       Position is primarily office/lab-based (Sunnyvale, CA). Requires regular access to prototype and lab environments with standard safety precautions. Up to 10% travel for clinical site visits, partner meetings, or conference participation.

Preferred Skills and Experience

•       Experience designing and implementing servo control systems, or a deeper robotics and controls background.

•       Medical device or safety-critical system product experience (FDA design controls, ISO 13485, ISO 14971).

•       Experience with surgical robotics, haptics, or tele-presence system design.

•       Familiarity with FPGA-based motor control or other embedded real-time architectures.

•       Experience developing products in a highly regulated environment, including through FDA clearance.

jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Rondo is accelerating industry’s transition to lower-cost, zero-carbon heat and power.

Our Rondo Heat Batteries turn low-cost renewable electricity into continuous, high-temperature heat and power, enabling industrial facilities to replace fossil-fired boilers without costly process changes. The result is lower-cost, zero-carbon industrial energy delivered safely, reliably, and at 98% efficiency.

Rondo is commercially deployed and rapidly scaling, today. Backed by world-class industrial leaders and investors — including Breakthrough Energy, Energy Impact Partners, Rio Tinto, Aramco, SABIC, SCG, TITAN, Microsoft, H&M, and John Doerr — Rondo is building the next generation of industrial energy infrastructure at global scale.

About the role

Rondo is developing its next-generation heat battery platform, now moving from concept into detailed design, validation builds, and first-of-a-kind deployment. As the Engineering Technical Program Manager for this platform, you run the engineering program day to day across more than a dozen subsystems. You turn gate targets into subsystem workplans, keep design maturity on track, and give the program lead an engineering schedule they can trust.

What You Will Do (key responsibilities for this role include but are not limited to):

• Own the program’s engineering schedule: subsystem workplans, design freeze dates, and engineering need-by dates, rolled into the program’s integrated schedule.

• Run the engineering cadence: weekly subsystem updates, design working sessions, and the engineering deliverables list for each gate.

• Plan and run subsystem design reviews: deliverables, reviewers and approvers, readiness, and action items through to closure.

• Track design maturity with subsystem leads and design managers: requirements and interfaces, analysis and verification plans, BOM maturity, and long-lead releases.

• Coordinate engineering inputs to manufacturing, supply chain, cost, and quality: BOMs, design-for-manufacture input, and build material needs.

• Run engineering decisions and risks day to day: frame design trade-offs with options and schedule impact, get them decided by the right subsystem leads and design managers on time, move them up the decision tiers when they stall, and keep engineering entries in the decision log and risk register current.

• Assess the schedule impact of design changes and interface issues, and bring options to design managers and the program lead.

• Prepare engineering readiness for phase gate reviews, working with the program lead who runs the gate.

• Improve engineering program tools: workplans, update templates, and design review checklists.

What You Bring

• 6+ years in engineering program or project management for complex hardware, including 2+ years running a multi-subsystem engineering program.

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, chemical, electrical, or systems engineering.

• Working knowledge of systems engineering: requirements management, interface control, design reviews, and verification planning.

• Experience taking hardware from concept through prototype and validation builds.

• Fluency with engineering data: BOMs, CAD and PDM structures, drawing release, and change control.

• Credibility with engineers: you follow a technical discussion, spot when a plan doesn’t add up, and get trade-offs framed and decided on time, escalating when they stall.

Bonus Points!

• Hands-on design or test experience in thermal, process, or power equipment, or industrial energy.

• Familiarity with requirements tools (Flow, Jama), Smartsheet, and PDM/PLM.

• Experience working alongside manufacturing and supply chain on new product introduction.

jobs.title: Safety Analysis Engineer II
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Safety Analysis Engineer II to help advance the development, testing, and deployment of Kaleidos, our portable, helium-cooled nuclear microreactor. With our first reactor built and production design underway, you'll work alongside a multidisciplinary team evaluating reactor safety, performance, and behavior under normal, transient, and accident conditions.

Depending on your technical background and program needs, your work could span reactor systems modeling, thermal hydraulics, accident analysis, fuel performance, source term development, and radiological consequence assessments. You'll have opportunities to evaluate safety margins, investigate reactor behavior, validate analytical models against test data, and help shape engineering decisions that support the safe design and deployment of Kaleidos.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own reactor safety analyses and evaluations that directly inform reactor design, safety margins, testing, and regulatory decisions.

 - Develop and apply engineering models to evaluate reactor behavior during normal operation, transients, and postulated accident scenarios.

 - Perform safety evaluations involving thermal hydraulics, fuel performance, source terms, radiological consequences, or other relevant areas.

 - Evaluate modeling assumptions, uncertainties, and sensitivities to establish technically defensible safety conclusions.

 - Collaborate with nuclear, mechanical, thermal, materials, and controls engineers to evaluate design alternatives and resolve safety-related technical challenges.

 - Support reactor testing by identifying validation requirements, reviewing experimental data, and comparing analytical predictions with test results.

 - Develop, validate, and improve safety analysis tools and methods, including Radiant's Digital Twin where applicable.

 - Prepare technical calculations, safety analysis reports, and documentation supporting reactor design, testing, and regulatory activities.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor's degree in nuclear engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field from an accredited institution.

 - 2+ years of relevant experience in reactor safety analysis, thermal hydraulics, nuclear systems modeling, or related engineering disciplines.

 - Technical depth in at least one area relevant to reactor safety, such as transient analysis, thermal hydraulics, fuel performance, source terms, or radiological consequences.

 - Experience using engineering calculations, simulation tools, or experimental data to evaluate reactor behavior, safety margins, or system performance.

 - Understanding of reactor safety fundamentals, including transient behavior, heat transfer, and the evaluation of engineering assumptions and uncertainties.

 - Ability to document technical analyses and communicate findings across engineering disciplines.


DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Master's degree or PhD in nuclear engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

 - Experience with high-temperature gas-cooled reactors, microreactors, advanced reactors, or TRISO fuel systems.

 - Experience with reactor safety analysis tools such as RELAP5-3D, TRACE, SAM, or MELCOR.

 - Familiarity with fuel performance, source term, or radiological consequence tools such as BISON, PARFUME, ORIGEN, or MACCS.

 - Experience with nuclear safety analysis methods, model verification and validation, uncertainty quantification, or probabilistic risk assessment.

 - Familiarity with DOE or NRC regulatory frameworks, safety basis development, reactor testing, or nuclear licensing activities.


ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

 - Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as necessary to accomplish our mission.

 - Must work 100% onsite at El Segundo HQ.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Nuclear Engineering Certificate Program: 100% covered educational program with Penn State University, for eligible employees, to rapidly upscale into nuclear.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s full-time new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.

jobs.description:
As a Communications Coordinator at GG Media, you will play an essential role in supporting internal and external communications, coordinating messaging initiatives, and ensuring that information is delivered clearly, consistently, and professionally.

This position is ideal for an organized, creative, and proactive individual who enjoys working with people, managing communication projects, and contributing to a dynamic business environment.

You will collaborate with different departments to maintain effective communication, support brand messaging, and help strengthen relationships with clients and business partners.

Key Responsibilities

• Coordinate and support daily internal and external communication activities.
• Draft, edit, and distribute professional correspondence, newsletters, announcements, and communication materials.
• Assist in developing and implementing communication strategies aligned with company objectives.
• Maintain consistent brand messaging across business communications and marketing materials.
• Collaborate with team members to organize communication campaigns, presentations, and company initiatives.
• Support client communication efforts and maintain positive professional relationships.
• Monitor communication timelines and ensure projects are completed accurately and efficiently.
• Prepare reports, presentations, and written materials for internal and external audiences.
• Identify opportunities to improve communication processes and overall effectiveness.
• Assist with event communications, promotional materials, and corporate announcements.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• Excellent organizational abilities and attention to detail.
• Creative thinking and the ability to communicate ideas effectively.
• Strong interpersonal skills and a professional, collaborative attitude.
• Ability to manage multiple projects and prioritize tasks efficiently.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, or similar productivity tools.
• Strong problem-solving skills and adaptability in a fast-paced environment.
• Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to team projects.
• A proactive mindset with a willingness to learn and develop new skills.
• Interest in corporate communications, brand development, and business strategy.

At GG Media, we recognize that our people are central to our success. We are committed to providing a workplace that encourages professional development, collaboration, and long-term growth.

• Competitive Salary: $50,000 – $56,000 annually.
• Career Growth Opportunities: Opportunities for professional advancement and increased responsibilities.
• Professional Development: Continuous learning and opportunities to strengthen communication, leadership, and organizational skills.
• Collaborative Environment: Work alongside a supportive, creative, and motivated team.
• Meaningful Projects: Contribute to communication initiatives that support business growth and brand development.
• Skill Enhancement: Develop valuable expertise in project coordination, business communication, and strategic planning.
• Dynamic Workplace: Enjoy a professional environment that values innovation, initiative, and fresh ideas.
• Long-Term Opportunities: Build a rewarding career with a company focused on continued growth

jobs.title: Lead Product Counsel
jobs.description:
About the role

We’re hiring a Lead Product Counsel to join Chime’s Legal team and advise on our lending and credit products. You’ll partner with Product, Compliance, Risk, Credit, Engineering, Design, and Operations to launch and grow products that help members access credit, while managing legal and regulatory risk. You’ll be a go-to advisor for lending and credit work on a close-knit legal team, bringing practical judgment, clear communication and strong relationships. This role is based in our San Francisco, Chicago or New York City office.

In this role, you can expect to

• Advise on Chime’s lending and credit products from early design through launch and beyond, spotting legal risk and giving practical, business-focused guidance.

• Translate federal and state lending and credit requirements into clear product, disclosure and operational requirements.

• Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Compliance, Risk, Credit and Operations so legal input shapes products early.

• Draft and review member-facing terms and conditions, disclosures and agreements for lending and credit products.

• Support Chime’s bank partnership programs, working through regulatory and partner requirements.

• Track regulatory and industry developments in consumer lending and help the business understand what they mean.

• Use outside counsel strategically and efficiently.

To thrive in this role, you have

• 5+ years of combined law firm, in-house and/or government experience, ideally including time in an in-house role.

• Hands-on experience counseling consumer lending or credit products at a fintech, a consumer tech company with a payments business, or a bank.

• Working knowledge of consumer lending and credit laws, such as TILA/Reg Z, ECOA/Reg B, FCRA/Reg V and UDAAP, and how they apply to product design.

• Sound judgment and concise communication: you can size a legal issue, prioritize risk and give non-lawyers a clear recommendation.

• Fluency with AI tools (such as Harvey, Glean, ChatGPT or Claude) to enhance work processes and outputs, with good judgment about verifying output and protecting confidential information.

• A JD from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing of a U.S. state bar.

#LI-Onsite #LI-LB1

Below is the base salary offered for this role and level of experience. Full-time employees may also be eligible for bonus(es), competitive equity, and benefits. For commissioned roles, the base salary listed in this job description does not include incentive/variable pay. The actual base salary offered may be higher, depending on your location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

Wage Notice

$177,000—$245,000 USD

A little about us

At Chime, we believe that everyone can achieve financial progress. We created Chime—a financial technology company, not a bank*—on the premise that core banking services should be helpful, easy, and free. Through our user-friendly tools and intuitive platforms, we empower our members to take control of their finances and work towards their goals. Whether it's starting a savings account, purchasing a first car or home, launching a business, or pursuing higher education, we're proud to have helped millions unlock their financial potential.

We're a team of problem solvers, dreamers, and builders with one shared obsession: our members. From day one, Chimers have worked tirelessly to out-hustle and out-execute competitors to bring our mission to life. Their grit and determination inspire us to work harder every day to deliver the very best experience possible. We each bring an owner's mindset to our work, refusing to be outdone and holding ourselves accountable to meet and exceed the highest bars for our teams, our company, and our members.

We believe in being bold, dreaming big, and taking risks, while also working together, embracing our diverse perspectives, and giving each other honest feedback. Our culture remains deeply entrepreneurial, encouraging every Chimer to see themselves as stewards of our mission to help everyday Americans unlock their financial progress.

We know that to achieve our mission, we must earn and keep people's trust—so we hold ourselves to the highest standards of integrity in everything we do. These aren't just words on a wall—our values are embedded in every aspect of our business, serving as a north star that guides us as we work to help millions achieve their financial potential.

Because if we don't—who will?

*Chime is a financial technology company, not a bank. Banking services provided by The Bancorp Bank, N.A. or Stride Bank, N.A., Members FDIC.

What we offer for our full-time, regular employees

• 🏢 Our in-office work policy is designed to keep you connected - with four days a week in the office and Fridays from home for those near one of our offices, plus team and company-wide events depending on location.

• 💻 Benefits that support your work and life, including backup child, elder, and pet care and subsidized commuter benefits for eligible employees.

• ✨ Comprehensive health, financial, and wellbeing benefits designed to support you at every stage of life.

• 🏝 Generous vacation policy and company-wide paid days off

• 👟 Annual wellness stipend to use towards eligible wellness related expenses

• 👪 Access to family planning reimbursement

We know that great work can’t be done without a diverse team and inclusive environment. That’s why we specifically look for individuals of varying strengths, skills, backgrounds, and ideas to join our team. We believe this gives us a competitive advantage to better serve our members and helps us all grow as Chimers and individuals.
