jobs.title: Lead Technical Program Manager, Robotics
jobs.description:
Persons in these roles are expected to work from our offices in Seattle. On-site requirements vary based on position and team. If you have questions about on-site work arrangements for this role, please ask your recruiter.

Our base salary range is $159,840 - $239,760, and in addition we have generous bonus plans to provide a competitive compensation package.

Who You Are:

You are someone who can make complicated, fast-moving technical work come together. You’re comfortable in the room with researchers and engineers, and you engage with the technical substance of what they’re building. Given a program with five workstreams, three external dependencies, and an ambitious release date, you can see clearly what has to happen and in what order. You’re direct about risk without being alarmist, and you would rather surface an uncomfortable tradeoff early than manage a surprise later. When work stalls or gaps appear, you first build collaborative relationships with the people involved and find creative ways forward, rather than add process. You have a good sense of how much structure a team actually needs, and you consider process a tool rather than a goal, adding it sparingly and dropping it proactively once it’s no longer serving the team. Research and engineering leaders seek out your judgment on how to structure ambitious, uncertain work, and you’re comfortable influencing senior leaders without formal authority. You’ve spent real time working with robotics, simulation, or other kinds of large-scale data pipelines, and that experience helps you spot when something like a sim-to-real gap or a slow data-generation loop is holding the program back.

Who We Are:

At Ai2, our mission is to develop breakthrough AI that solves the world's biggest problems. We believe the insight needed to get there lives at the intersection of deep scientific AI understanding and applying AI in common-good domains. This role sits on our Strategic Programs team, which also includes Product Management, Design, and Communications. As a team, we help shape Ai2's strategic vision and accelerate execution of its goals. We are a highly collaborative team with a high bar for excellence, and we aren't afraid to question how things have been done in the past to propose changes that drive the organization forward. It's a very exciting time to be part of this team as Ai2 plays a unique role in shaping how AI changes the world.

Your Next Challenge:

You will lead program structure and execution for Ai2's Robotics team, headed by Dieter Fox. In 2027, the team will extend its existing frameworks into a single open framework for data generation, training, evaluation, and sim-to-real transfer, and build high-precision domain capabilities for specific real-world research tasks, validated on real hardware with external scientific partners. This framework is built to help answer some of the most fundamental open questions in robotics, such as how best to bridge low-level dexterous control with high-level reasoning, how data, model architectures, and training regimes combine to produce capable robots, and what specifically stands between today's systems and broad, general competence. You'll make these concurrent efforts add up to one coherent plan, keep scope appropriate against stretch goals, and turn research progress into open releases the community can build on.

You’ll be accountable for how well the program holds together and operates as a whole. That means a flexible, robust plan that adapts as research evolves, a shared picture of progress leaders can easily understand, and a team empowered to focus on the research itself. You’ll also be a senior voice in how program management works across Ai2, mentoring other TPMs and building frameworks other programs adopt.

Robotics is your first and primary focus. As Ai2's priorities shift, you'll also be expected to take on program work in other areas, such as model training, scientific agents, geospatial AI, or the infrastructure that supports them. We're looking for someone who is energized by new problems and who can step into an unfamiliar technical area and become effective quickly.

In This Role, You Will:

• Define the program structure and own end-to-end execution across Robotics' concurrent workstreams, deciding how work is organized, sequenced, and governed rather than inheriting a structure, and driving the program to its committed outcomes.

• Establish and run the operating cadence for your programs, calibrating them as the needs of the team evolve to maximize useful connections and communication and minimize friction.

• Forecast compute and storage for your programs, such as simulation data generation and model training, and secure capacity with our AI infrastructure team before it becomes a bottleneck.

• Identify, communicate, and drive resolution of dependencies and risks across teams, using judgment about which issues to resolve directly and which to escalate, and bringing trade-off recommendations to research and senior leadership.

• Own reporting obligations for your programs, which may include quarterly business reviews, funder reporting, and recurring updates to Ai2 leadership, and represent the program's execution health to Ai2 leadership.

• Coordinate open releases of assets, scene and task generators, datasets, models, and training recipes, including asset licensing, documentation, and benchmark readiness, so external researchers can reproduce and extend our work.

• Coordinate with Communications, Product, and research leads to ensure external releases are communicated effectively and received well by intended audiences and the wider world.

• Notice where your programs overlap with others across Ai2 and turn those overlaps into proposals for shared tooling, joint evaluation, or research threads that serve both teams.

• Structure cross-team and external support, including engineers on loan from other Ai2 teams and advisory partners like wet-lab collaborators, with clear scope, timelines, and handoffs.

• Where relevant, partner closely with Product Management, who own what we build and for whom, while you own how the org plans, executes, and delivers on it. Work through ambiguous use cases directly with your product counterpart.

• Extend into other Ai2 programs as needs arise, bringing the structure and practices that work in Robotics to adjacent teams and contributing to the overall planning, release, and reporting practices of our program management function.

What You’ll Need:

• 12+ years of relevant experience with a bachelor's degree, or 8+ years with an advanced degree, in technical program management, engineering program management, or a closely related role, including programs spanning multiple teams and technical domains.

• Demonstrated technical depth in robotics, simulation, ML data pipelines, or ML infrastructure, and the breadth to apply that judgment to other ML research programs. You don't need to be a roboticist, but you should be able to reason about tradeoffs like simulation fidelity versus throughput, data scale versus quality, or evaluation in simulation versus on real hardware.

• Experience migrating or unifying multiple technical platforms.

• A track record of designing and leading multiple complex technical programs on committed timelines, including at least one where the plan had to change substantially mid-flight.

• Clear, audience-aware written communication, with the ability to produce status updates, risk escalations, and planning docs that people read and act on.

• Excellent stakeholder management across research, engineering, and organizational functions such as legal, finance, and communications, including with senior leaders.

• Comfort operating with ambiguity, building frameworks and processes where none exist yet, and knowing which processes are worth the overhead.

• Genuine interest in AI research and its applications, and the adaptability to learn a new technical domain quickly.

Nice To Have:

• Experience in a research organization, national lab, or academic environment, where timelines and incentives differ from a product company.

• Familiarity with open model or open data releases, and the coordination they require across research, legal, and communications.

• Familiarity with robot simulation tools (e.g., MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, ManiSkill) or robot learning workflows such as teleoperation, demonstration data, and policy evaluation.

• Experience with lab automation, life sciences, or other high-precision manipulation settings.

• Experience running programs that combine physical hardware or lab operations with software, and the planning that hardware lead times and lab constraints can require.

• Experience managing infrastructure-constrained programs, such as compute or storage capacity planning, allocation across competing teams, or vendor coordination.

• Experience mentoring or coaching other program or project managers, formally or informally.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions.

• Must be able to remain in a stationary position for long periods of time.

• The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.

• The ability to observe details at close range.

• Can work under deadlines.

A Little More About Ai2:

Ai2 is a Seattle based non-profit AI research institute founded in 2014 by the late Paul Allen. Our mission is building breakthrough AI to solve the world’s biggest problems. We develop foundational AI research and innovation to deliver real-world impact through large-scale open models, data, robotics, conservation, and beyond.

In addition to Ai2’s core mission, we also aim to contribute to humanity through our treatment of each member of the Ai2 Team. Some highlights are:

• We are a learning organization – because everything Ai2 does is ground-breaking, we are learning every day. With a wide variety of world-class AI experts as guest speakers, and our commitment to your personal on-going education, Ai2 is a place where you will have opportunities to continue learning alongside your coworkers.

• We value diversity - We seek to hire, support, and promote people from all genders, ethnicities, and all levels of experience regardless of age. We particularly encourage applications from women, non-binary individuals, people of color, members of the LGBTQA+ community, and people with disabilities of any kind.

• We value inclusion - We understand the value that people's individual experiences and perspectives can bring to an organization, and we are building a culture in which all voices are heard, respected and considered.

• We emphasize a healthy work/life balance – we believe our team members are happiest and most productive when their work/life balance is optimized. While we value powerful research results which drive our mission forward, we also value dinner with family, weekend time, and vacation time. We offer generous paid vacation and sick leave as well as family leave.

• We are collaborative and transparent – we consider ourselves a team, all moving with a common purpose. We are quick to cheer our successes, and even quicker to share and jointly problem solve our failures.

• We are in Seattle – and our office is on the water! We have mountains, we have lakes, we have four seasons, we bike to work, we have a vibrant theater scene, and we have so much else. We welcome interest from applicants from outside of the United States.

• We are friendly– chances are you will like every one of the 200+ (and growing) people who work here. We do.

Ai2 is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. Employers can only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to employees and applicants with disabilities to the full extent required by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). If you feel you need a reasonable accommodation pursuant to the ADA, you are encouraged to contact us at recruiting@allenai.org.

Benefits:

• Team members are able to enroll in our health savings account plan, our healthcare reimbursement arrangement plan, and our health care and dependent care flexible spending account plans.

• Team members are able to enroll in our company’s 401k plan.

jobs.title: Director, Analytical Development
jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

This leadership role will provide strategic and operational oversight for Analytical Development within the PDM organization, leading analytical strategies and execution to support Revolution Medicines’ pipeline and clinical programs. Responsibilities include oversight of analytical method development, validation, transfer, release and stability testing, regulatory support, and management of external partners to enable phase appropriate development and commercialization readiness.

• Provide strategic and organizational leadership for analytical development activities supporting small molecule API and drug product development, including oversight of phase appropriate control strategies, specification setting, analytical lifecycle management, and overall CMC analytical strategy.

• Lead and oversee analytical development execution across internal and external teams to support the development, characterization, and manufacturing of API and drug product, while actively contributing to cross functional PDM project teams.

• Provide strategic guidance and oversight for regulatory submission activities, including authoring and review Quality sections of regulatory submissions, and leading responses to regulatory queries.

• Establish and drive analytical strategies, technology selection, and operational execution through effective management of CDMOs, CROs, and contract laboratories, with accountability for quality, timelines, risk management, and delivery.

• Provide leadership oversight for preparation, review, and approval of analytical protocols, reports, specifications, investigations, and technical documentation to ensure scientific excellence, regulatory compliance, and inspection readiness.

• Build strong cross functional partnerships and influence across Drug Product, Drug Substance, Regulatory Affairs, QA, Project Management, Medicinal Chemistry, DMPK, Toxicology and senior leadership teams to drive strategic decision making and achievement of program and organizational goals.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

• PhD preferred (minimum MS) in Analytical Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, or a related scientific discipline.

• 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in analytical development within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

• Proven ability to lead cross functional teams, influence organizational decision making, and drive execution of complex development strategies in a matrix environment.

• Extensive strategic and operational leadership experience overseeing analytical activities across small molecule drug development, with strong preference for late phase development, regulatory approval, and commercialization readiness.

• Excellent communication, collaboration, people leadership, and stakeholder management skills.

• Deep understanding of CMC strategies and analytical enablement for small molecule development programs.

• Demonstrated leadership experience managing external partners, including CROs and CDMOs, to ensure high-quality deliverables and program execution.

• Strong knowledge of global regulatory requirements and experience supporting regulatory submissions, including INDs, IMPDs, NDAs, and/or MAAs.

• In-depth understanding of ICH guidelines, GMP regulations, and current industry best practices related to analytical development and quality.

• Strong strategic thinking and innovation mindset with the ability to independently evaluate complex issues, identify risks, and implement effective solutions.

• Ability to prioritize and lead multiple initiatives in a fast paced, dynamic, and highly collaborative environment.

Preferred Skills:

• Experience leveraging AI tools to streamline workflows, automate repetitive tasks, and enhance team productivity.

• Experience in analytical method development for biologics.

jobs.title: Senior Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
About AiDASH

AiDASH is leading the PreventionFirst™movement for electric utilities and transforming grid resilience through its pioneering platform that unifies vegetation, asset, storm, and wildfire intelligence. Powered by SatelliteFirst™ Inspection & Monitoring, AiDASH delivers comprehensive visibility across the entire grid at the right frequency and budget, using the right data modality. More than 200 customers trust AiDASH to keep the lights on, spend where it counts, and defend every decision, Securing Tomorrow across every mile of the grid. Learn more at www.aidash.com.

The PreventionFirst movement is growing, and so is the recognition behind it. In 2026, Forbes named AiDASH one of America's Best Startup Employers for the 4th consecutive year, and TIME included AiDASH among America's Top GreenTech Companies for the 3rd year in a row. Deloitte Technology Fast 500™ ranked AiDASH No. 12 in the San Francisco Bay Area, and No. 59 overall in their selection of the top 500 for 2024.

Join us in Securing Tomorrow Together!

The Role

AiDASH is helping electric utilities and infrastructure providers improve reliability, reduce risk, and make smarter decisions for their operations. Our SaaS platform combines satellite data, analytics, and practical insights to support critical day-to-day work like vegetation management and storm preparedness.

We're looking for a Senior Customer Success Manager (CSM) to drive long-term success for our strategic North American customers. As the primary point of contact for a portfolio of active SaaS accounts, you'll own customer satisfaction, engagement, and retention - ensuring our customers consistently realize value from our platform. You’ll build trusted relationships across all levels, from field managers to executive stakeholders, becoming a go-to partner in their day-to-day operations and long-term planning. You’ll join a high-impact Customer Success team made up of CSMs, Product Consultants, and Project Managers - all committed to delivering measurable outcomes together.

You’ll be joining a high-performing Customer Success team that includes CSMs, Product Consultants, and PMs who work closely together to deliver outcomes. This is a relationship-driven role suited for someone who thrives in high-ownership environments, enjoys supporting real-world operations, and brings strong follow-through to everything they do.

Why AiDASH?

Our customers are on the front lines of the energy transition, climate adaptation, and infrastructure modernization. This role gives you a seat at the table with decision-makers who are responsible for keeping the lights on, managing vegetation risk, and meeting regulatory standards. You’ll join a team that’s collaborative, mission-focused, and committed to delivering outcomes that matter.

We’re also growing fast. This role offers a path to expand your impact - whether deepening relationships in strategic accounts, mentoring others, or helping shape the future of customer experience at AiDASH.

If you care about helping customers succeed and want to work on meaningful infrastructure challenges, we’d love to hear from you!

How you'll make an impact:

• Own a portfolio of multi-year AiDASH customers, driving deep engagement, strong adoption, and long-term retention

• Build and maintain trusted relationships with customer stakeholders across field teams, operations, and leadership

• Lead regular check-ins, training sessions, and strategic planning meetings to keep customers informed, aligned, and empowered

• Monitor product usage, customer health, and feedback to proactively surface risks and uncover new opportunities

• Collaborate closely with Product Consultants, Project Managers, Support, and Sales to solve challenges and improve customer outcomes

• Play a key role in renewals and expansion efforts, working hand-in-hand with Sales to grow customer value and impact

What we're looking for:

• 6+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, or related post-sales roles within B2B SaaS or infrastructure sectors

• Strong communication and relationship-building skills across all levels of the customer organization - from field managers to senior executives

• Highly organized and dependable, with a proven ability to manage multiple accounts and competing priorities effectively

• Quick learner and confident in explaining software platforms and data dashboards to diverse audiences

• Experience working with utilities, infrastructure operators, or field-heavy industries is a strong plus

What you'll love:

• Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage: 100% coverage for employees and 80% for their spouses and children

• Health Reimbursement Account (HRA): 100% funded by AiDASH to cover medical deductibles

• 401(k) Plan: Begin contributing after three months of employment to prepare for your future. Currently, no company match is offered

• Parental Leave: Supportive parental leave with 16 weeks for primary caregivers and 4 weeks for secondary caregivers

• Generous Vacation Policy: Accrue 20 vacation days per year, plus enjoy an additional flex holiday to celebrate whatever feels most important to you.

• Winter Break: From December 25th through January 1st, we give everyone time off to recharge and enjoy time with family and friends!

We are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to embracing diversity and inclusion in our hiring practices, and we promote a work environment where everyone, from any race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin, can do their best work.

We offer a competitive annual pay range of $110,000 to $140,000 for this full-time position, which includes a base salary and bonus based on performance. This range reflects the anticipated annual pay range (base + bonus) for new hires. We strive to ensure our compensation packages are equitable and aligned with industry standards. Your recruiter can share more about compensation during the hiring process.

We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible interview experience for all candidates. Please let us know if you require any accommodation during the interview process, and we will make every effort to meet your needs.

jobs.description:
Everpure (NYSE: P) has evolved from storage pioneer to data platform, closing fiscal 2026 with $3.7 billion in revenue, its first billion-dollar quarter, and accelerating growth into FY27. Our strategic agenda spans the companies defining the next era of technology - hyperscalers, AI labs, the AI hardware supply chain, data platform providers, and the broader AI ecosystem.

This type of work—work that changes the world—is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

THE ROLE

Portworx by Everpure is the leading global solution for unlocking the potential of Kubernetes by unlocking the power of data at enterprise scale.  Portworx is a cloud native platform that enterprises depend on to reduce the cost and complexity of rapidly deploying containerized applications across multiple clouds and on-prem environments.  By providing a single standard that works across the environment, we reduce the operating cost of kubernetes, unlock more use cases, respond and pivot to changes due to economic, regulatory and/or business impacts and make it easier to modernize applications, delight developers, and deliver innovation.

Via Portworx, you can manage any database or stateful service on any infrastructure using any container scheduler. You get a single data management layer for all of your stateful services, no matter where they run. And we thrive in multi-cloud environments.

We are looking for Kubernetes experts to help our team capture this massive and rapidly growing market opportunity.  This architect role will serve as the vanguard of the “Kubernetes Everywhere” movement. There’s no safe harbor here for those that can’t, don't, or won’t. There’s also no room for those that put “I” ahead of “We”.

We are customer first, we lead with integrity, and recognize that unlocking achievement requires engagement across the full spectrum of co-selling partners. We are builders, creators, and helping define the next generation of the world’s best modern data platform at Pure.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

The Portworx Cloud Native Architect is a customer-facing role responsible for providing deep technical and business expertise to customers who want to run stateful applications in containers and automate “Day 2” data management workflows.

WHAT YOU BRING:

• 5+ years' experience as a customer facing senior-level technical architect.

• Charismatic, confident, and likable self-starter with a track record of success on stage, in the spotlight, and with customers.

• Team oriented leader that is able to coach and drive desired behavior through influence rather than title.

• 5+ years of Linux Administration and/or Linux development experience with an industry recognized administration-level or higher certification.

• Certification-level fluency with DevOps concepts and hands-on experience with associated tools, such as; Ansible, Terraform, Docker, and CI/CD pipeline applications.

• Certification-level fluency in data engineering, big data, and database operations, delivery and operational services.

• Demonstrable understanding of data platform technologies as they relate to highly available business applications on-prem, hybrid, and in the cloud

• Demonstrable understanding of the enterprise application development lifecycle and container platforms’ effect on it.

• Demonstrable ability to see and present ‘the big picture’ e.g. thought leadership, offer solutions to improve upon it, and challenge the status quo when it is not in alignment with or in the best interest of desired customer outcomes.

• Demonstrable ability to distill complex problems into a simplified vision that drives customer interest in Everpure technologies

jobs.title: Director, Brand Strategy
jobs.description:
This role can be based in either our New York, Bay Area (SF or South Bay) or Seattle office.

At LinkedIn, our approach to flexible work is centered on trust and optimized for culture, connection, clarity, and the evolving needs of our business. The work location of this role is hybrid, meaning it will be performed both from home and from a LinkedIn office on select days, as determined by the business needs of the team.

Corporate Brand Marketing is looking for a Director, Brand Strategy to shape what LinkedIn stands for in a new era of work and ensure it comes through in everything we say, do, and make.

Reporting to the VP, Corporate Brand Marketing, this role calls for vision, creativity, and a bias for action. Strategy is your craft, but your impact comes from the conviction you bring, the bar you raise, and your ability to turn a fast-moving business into a clear and compelling brand story.

You’ll lead LinkedIn’s brand strategy end-to-end, then put it to work across the business. Working alongside creative, marketing, product, and senior leaders, you’ll make our brand sharper, more distinctive, and ready for where LinkedIn is going next.

Responsibilities

• Lead LinkedIn’s brand strategy across the company, businesses and products.

• Turn our brand promise, positioning, architecture, messaging, and expression into a clear, useful system.

• Start with the business problem, using audience, cultural and competitive insight to shape strategy and priorities.

• Lead positioning, value propositions and naming that make LinkedIn’s value clear and differentiation visible.

• Build a high-performing team, raise the strategic bar and connect brand thinking to stronger creative and marketing.

• Use audience insights and brand measurement to guide decisions and demonstrate business impact.

• Shape critical brand decisions with senior leaders and lead the strategy behind LinkedIn’s most important brand initiatives.

• Create clarity across a complex organization by aligning teams, resolving trade-offs and advancing one LinkedIn brand.

Basic Qualifications

• 10+ years of experience in brand strategy, with at least 5 years in a people leadership role
• BA/BS degree in marketing, business, or related field, or equivalent practical experience

Preferred Qualifications

jobs.title: Thermo-Mechanical Engineer II
jobs.description:
About Us

At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space.



The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy.

About the Role

As the Thermal-Mechanical Engineer for Integration of the Power Conversion System (PCS), you will own how heat moves through the Power Conversion System, including the thermal budget and its impact on hardware over time. Your scope runs from the thermal energy budget of the whole system down to the insulation on a single hot-section joint. You will develop the heat rejection and cold-sink architecture that closes the cycle, size and integrate the recuperator, define the thermal configuration of the hot section (insulation, heat-loss budget, surface temperatures, and personnel protection), and hold the thermal interfaces and transient requirements against the major PCS components, the reactor, and the safety systems. You are responsible for managing temperature-related life-limited hardware including mitigations, inspection procedures and processes, and a maintenance plan that manages that risk.  You will participate in testing and data reviews for test rigs, full-scale hardware, and deployed reactors. You will drive instrumentation placement, correlate your models against what the PCS actually does, and take the delta back into the design.

The ideal candidate is fluent in heat transfer across conduction, convection, and radiation, has sized real thermal hardware rather than only analyzed it, and is comfortable owning the heat-loss budget and the cold-sink margin and working with component owners to ensure thermal performance is met. Experience with high-temperature power cycles, creep and thermal-mechanical fatigue life, or bringing first-of-a-kind hardware through thermal commissioning is a strong differentiator.



Key Responsibilities:

 - Own thermal management and thermal energy budget of the Power Conversion System and close the loop with cycle performance on parasitic losses.

 - Develop the heat rejection and cold-sink architecture, sizing and integrating the recuperator and heat rejection against site and ambient conditions.

 - Define the thermal configuration including insulation selection and design, heat-loss budget, surface temperatures, instrumentation, and personnel protection.

 - Manage thermal interfaces and thermal transient requirements for major PCS components, reactor, and safety systems.

 - Support test rig design and instrumentation placement. Utilize collected data to improve component life and performance.

 - Engineer components for high-temperature and high-stress service using metals and advanced materials, in partnership with materials and structural analysis.

 - Work with the team to develop inspection and maintenance plans that manage risk on thermal-mechanically life-limited.

 - Work with Mechanical, Electrical, Safety, and Nuclear teams to ensure the designs meet the overall objectives and requirements.

Basic Qualifications:

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Nuclear, or a related engineering discipline

 - 2+ years of full-cycle engineering experience for Engineer II

 - Experience performing thermal analysis (hand calculations and FEA or CFD) to size, configure, or qualify hardware

 - Experience designing thermal management hardware for high-temperature systems, such as insulation systems, heat-loss budgets, or thermal isolation

 - Experience sizing or integrating heat exchangers or a heat rejection path against real operating and ambient conditions

 - Experience correlating thermal predictions against test data and revising a design based on the result

 - Experience owning thermal interfaces or requirements across multiple subsystems

Preferred Skills & Experience:

 - Experience in the Nuclear, Aerospace, Automotive, Power Generation, Motorsports, or Oil and Gas industries

 - Experience with recuperators, air-cooled or dry heat rejection, and ambient-dependent performance derating

 - Experience selecting and designing high-temperature insulation systems, including hot-face and cold-face design and personnel-protection surface temperature limits

 - Experience with transient thermal analysis of startup, shutdown, trip, and off-nominal cases

 - Experience with thermal-mechanical fatigue, creep, and creep-fatigue interaction, and with life assessment of temperature-limited components

 - Experience with elevated-temperature design codes such as ASME BPVC Section III Division 5 or Section VIII Division 2 Part 5

 - Experience with high-temperature metals and advanced materials, including nickel superalloys and their creep-limited allowable

 - Experience specifying thermal instrumentation (thermocouple and RTD selection, placement, and measurement uncertainty) and using it to correlate models

 - Experience developing inspection and maintenance plans for life-limited hardware, including NDE method selection

 - Experience with thermal and structural analysis tools such as ANSYS Mechanical, Femap or NX Thermal, and/or CFD tools such as Fluent or Star-CCM+

 - Experience commissioning first-of-a-kind hardware and supporting thermal startup and troubleshooting

 - Experience in a demanding, fast-paced development environment

Additional Requirements:

 - Ability to work long hours and weekends as necessary to support critical milestones.

Location:

 - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access

Salary Range:

 - Thermo-Mechanical Engineer II - $118,000 - $155,000



Culture

At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful:

 - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system

 - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle

 - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done”

 - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together

 - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption
   
   

Equal Opportunity

Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.  - Design and analyze heat exchanger inlet/outlet piping, manifolds, and associated mechanical interfaces, ensuring compatibility with system performance and installation requirements.

 - Evaluate thermal stresses, differential thermal expansion, pressure loads, piping flexibility, and mechanical loads transmitted between heat exchangers, piping, and supporting structures.

 - Support development of manufacturing methods, including material selection, fabrication processes, joining techniques, and assembly of heat exchanger and piping components.

 - Design and support development of test articles, test stands, and procedures to validate thermal performance, structural integrity, and operational life.

 - Coordinate with internal teams and external stakeholders to translate system requirements into manufacturable and reliable hardware products.

 - Support the design and integration of piping connections, flanges, weld joints, supports, and other fluid-system components, considering manufacturability, assembly, inspection, and maintenance.

 - Define operating limits and performance envelopes for heat exchanger systems.

 - Investigate hardware failures, identify root causes, and rapidly implement design improvements to enhance performance and reliability.

 - 5+ years of experience in mechanical or thermal engineering, preferably involving heat exchangers, pressure-containing equipment, or high-temperature systems.

 - Demonstrated experience with mechanical CAD design and engineering analysis tools (e.g., SolidWorks, NX, ANSYS, COMSOL).

 - Understanding of heat transfer fundamentals, fluid mechanics, thermal stresses, and structural mechanics.

 - Understanding of piping and pressure-containing component design, including pressure loads, thermal expansion, and mechanical interfaces.

 - Knowledge of materials science as it applies to material selection, thermal properties, and structural performance.

 - Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or Thermal Sciences.

 - Demonstrated experience in heat exchanger design, analysis, manufacturing, and testing.

 - Experience with high-temperature (500°C+) systems, including thermal expansion, creep, fatigue, and material compatibility considerations.

 - Experience with thermal and structural finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).

 - Experience designing high-temperature piping systems, manifolds, and associated mechanical components.

 - Experience evaluating piping flexibility, thermal stresses, and loads at equipment connections using analytical or simulation tools.

 - Familiarity with heat exchanger and piping fabrication methods, including welding, brazing, and other joining processes.

 - Understanding of nuclear safety standards, quality requirements, and regulatory considerations.

jobs.title: People Project Manager
jobs.description:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft is changing fast. We’re integrating acquired businesses, growing in Europe and new global markets, launching new lines of business, and building a workforce for autonomous vehicles alongside our corporate teams. Half of our team members now live outside the US. Our People team has to keep pace, and that means designing programs that work for a bigger, more global and more varied Lyft.

The People Strategy & Programs team leads complex, cross-functional work that comes to the People organization. We run the People team’s operating rhythms and make sure our biggest priorities get delivered across every People vertical: HR Operations, Total Rewards, Talent Acquisition, Team Member Experience and People Business Partners.

As People Project Manager, you’ll own high-complexity programs end to end as the People team transforms alongside the business. You’ll report to the Chief of Staff to the Chief People Officer and partner closely with People leaders, Finance, Legal and business leaders across Lyft. This isn’t a role where you hand work off once the plan is set. You’ll facilitate the strategy, validate it with subject matter experts, lead when the work needs a leader, and get into the details to keep it moving.

This role is for a systems thinker who’s comfortable with ambiguity and enjoys every part of the People function. Success looks like complex programs that land well, People leaders who see you as a trusted partner, and repeatable approaches that make the next big project easier than the last.

What you’ll work on:
Your portfolio will shift with the business, but example programs include:

• Standing up People programs for new and growing workforces, such as hourly and field teams

• Partnering with the business on workforce and location strategy: the right roles in the right places at the right cost

• Driving AI and automation adoption across the People team, from prioritization through measuring impact

• Designing org structures and ways of working built for speed and scale, from spans and layers to decision rights and our matrix model

What success looks like:

• By month 3: Owning 1 - 3 active programs with clear plans, owners, metrics and status reporting in place

• By month 6: Leading at least one major cross-functional program, such as an integration or org design effort, with minimal oversight

• By month 12: Recognized by People leaders as the go-to partner for complex, cross-functional work, with at least one repeatable playbook or framework in use across the team

Responsibilities:

• Owning complex, cross-functional People programs from scoping through delivery, defining strategy, milestones and success metrics, and adapting plans as business needs change

• Turning ambiguous problems into clear, actionable plans, and working through options independently before escalating

• Facilitating strategy discussions with People and business leaders, and validating recommendations with subject matter experts across the People team

• Building strong relationships with senior leaders and assembling the right cross-functional teams to deliver

• Developing executive-ready deliverables, including decks, recommendations, decision documents and change communications

• Leading change management for org changes, integrations and new programs, including stakeholder management, change readiness assessments, manager preparation and coordination with internal communications

• Synthesizing data across programs to weigh short-term trade-offs against long-term goals and influence scope and strategy

• Creating scalable program plans, templates and project management standards so People teams run work the same way

• Getting into the details when needed to remove blockers and keep work moving

• Handling sensitive and confidential information with discretion

Experience:

• 7+ years of experience across program management, HR business partnering, HR generalist work, management consulting or business operations

• HR business partner, People business partner or HR generalist experience strongly preferred, with a broad understanding of how People functions work together

• Consulting experience preferred, especially in organizational design, change management or transformation

• Track record owning complex, cross-functional programs end to end in ambiguous environments

• Experience influencing senior leaders and building alignment across teams with competing priorities

• Strong problem-solving and systems thinking, with the ability to see how decisions in one area affect others

• Excellent written communication and experience creating executive-level materials

• Comfort using data to measure progress and support recommendations

• Experience with M&A integration, restructuring or global expansion preferred

• Experience using AI tools to improve how work gets done

Benefits:

• Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled

• Mental health benefits

• Family building benefits

• Child care and pet benefits

• 401(k) plan with company match to help save for your future

• In addition to 12 observed holidays, salaried team members have discretionary paid time off, hourly team members have 15 days paid time off

• 18 weeks of paid parental leave. Biological, adoptive, and foster parents are all eligible

• Subsidized commuter benefits

• Monthly Lyft credits and complimentary Lyft Pink membership

Lyft is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other basis prohibited by law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.

Lyft highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture. This role will be in-office on a hybrid schedule following the establishment of a Lyft office in Nashville — Team Members will be expected to work in the office 3 days per week on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. Lyft considers working in the office at least 3 days per week to be an essential function of this hybrid role. Additionally, hybrid roles have the flexibility to work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year. #Hybrid

The expected base pay range for this position in the Nashville area is $108,240 - $135,300, not inclusive of potential equity offering, bonus or benefits. Salary ranges are dependent on a variety of factors, including qualifications, experience and geographic location. Your recruiter can share more information about the salary range specific to your working location and other factors during the hiring process.

We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space.



The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy.

About the Role

As a Thermo-Mechanical Design Engineer, you will play a key role in developing, designing, qualifying, and deploying advanced heat exchanger systems for cutting-edge energy applications. You will work closely with Responsible Engineers and cross-functional teams to mature designs from concept through production. The ideal candidate will bring strong mechanical design fundamentals, thermal engineering knowledge, and hands-on hardware development experience to deliver reliable, high-performance heat exchangers and associated piping systems for next-generation energy applications.



Roles & Responsibilities

 - Perform mechanical design, modeling, and analysis of heat exchanger systems, ensuring thermal performance, structural integrity, and compatibility with system interfaces.

 - Design and analyze heat exchanger inlet/outlet piping, manifolds, and associated mechanical interfaces, ensuring compatibility with system performance and installation requirements.

 - Evaluate thermal stresses, differential thermal expansion, pressure loads, piping flexibility, and mechanical loads transmitted between heat exchangers, piping, and supporting structures.

 - Support development of manufacturing methods, including material selection, fabrication processes, joining techniques, and assembly of heat exchanger and piping components.

 - Design and support development of test articles, test stands, and procedures to validate thermal performance, structural integrity, and operational life.

 - Coordinate with internal teams and external stakeholders to translate system requirements into manufacturable and reliable hardware products.

 - Support the design and integration of piping connections, flanges, weld joints, supports, and other fluid-system components, considering manufacturability, assembly, inspection, and maintenance.

 - Define operating limits and performance envelopes for heat exchanger systems.

 - Investigate hardware failures, identify root causes, and rapidly implement design improvements to enhance performance and reliability.

Basic Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related physics-based field.

 - 2+ years of experience in mechanical or thermal engineering, preferably involving heat exchangers, pressure-containing equipment, or high-temperature systems.

 - Demonstrated experience with mechanical CAD design and engineering analysis tools (e.g., SolidWorks, NX, ANSYS, COMSOL).

 - Understanding of heat transfer fundamentals, fluid mechanics, thermal stresses, and structural mechanics.

 - Understanding of piping and pressure-containing component design, including pressure loads, thermal expansion, and mechanical interfaces.

 - Knowledge of materials science as it applies to material selection, thermal properties, and structural performance.

Preferred Skills and Experience

 - Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or Thermal Sciences.

 - Demonstrated experience in heat exchanger design, analysis, manufacturing, and testing.

 - Experience with high-temperature (500°C+) systems, including thermal expansion, creep, fatigue, and material compatibility considerations.

 - Experience with thermal and structural finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD).

 - Experience designing high-temperature piping systems, manifolds, and associated mechanical components.

 - Experience evaluating piping flexibility, thermal stresses, and loads at equipment connections using analytical or simulation tools.

 - Familiarity with heat exchanger and piping fabrication methods, including welding, brazing, and other joining processes.

 - Experience designing pressure-containing components and familiarity with applicable ASME codes and standards (e.g., ASME BPVC Section VIII, ASME B31.1, or B31.3).

 - Experience developing and executing hardware validation tests, including pressure, thermal cycling, and performance testing.

 - Understanding of nuclear safety standards, quality requirements, and regulatory considerations.

 - Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, manufacturing, materials, quality, and testing teams.

Additional Requirements:

 - Ability to work long hours and weekends as necessary to support critical milestones.

Location:

 - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access

Salary Range:

 - Thermo-Mechanical Design Engineer II - $118,000 - $155,000



Culture

At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful:

 - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system

 - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle

 - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done”

 - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together

 - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption
   
   

Equal Opportunity

Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.




ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jobs.title: People Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft is changing fast. We’re integrating acquired businesses, growing in Europe and new global markets, launching new lines of business, and building a workforce for autonomous vehicles alongside our corporate teams. Half of our team members now live outside the US. Our People team has to keep pace, and that means designing programs that work for a bigger, more global and more varied Lyft.

The People Strategy & Programs team leads complex, cross-functional work that comes to the People organization. We run the People team’s operating rhythms and make sure our biggest priorities get delivered across every People vertical: HR Operations, Total Rewards, Talent Acquisition, Team Member Experience and People Business Partners.

As People Project Coordinator, you’ll own the operating rhythm and budget of the People team, including annual planning, OKRs and quarterly business reviews. You’ll also own workstreams within larger People programs, such as change management for a major cross-functional project or business initiative with large people impacts. You’ll report to the Chief of Staff to the Chief People Officer and work closely with People leaders and partners across the team.

This role is for a problem solver who can run independently, build strong deliverables and keep work moving. You’ll coordinate across teams, develop materials leaders rely on, and track progress so nothing falls through the cracks. Over time, you’ll take on more facilitation and cross-functional work. Success looks like People team rhythms that run smoothly, workstreams that deliver on time, and leaders who trust your materials and updates.

What you’ll work on:

• Run the People team’s operating rhythm, including annual planning, OKR setting and tracking, quarterly business reviews and People leadership team meetings

• Run the People team budget, including tracking spend, forecasting and partnering with Finance

• Own workstreams within larger People programs, such as change management for a major cross-functional project or business initiative with large people impacts

• Step into cross-functional gray areas where roles and responsibilities get blurry, and helping teams define ownership quickly

What success looks like:

• By month 3: Running core People team rhythms independently, including OKR tracking, budget tracking and quarterly business review preparation

• By month 6: Owning 2 - 3 workstreams within cross-functional projects, with clear plans and regular status reporting

• By month 12: Leading the full annual planning and budget cycle for the People team and recognized as a reliable partner for coordination and execution

Responsibilities:

• Owning the planning and execution of People team rhythms, from calendars and pre-reads to follow-ups and action tracking

• Partnering with People leaders to set OKRs, track progress and flag risks before they become problems

• Managing the People team budget, tracking spend against plan and flagging variances early

• Managing workstream plans, milestones and status updates within larger programs, and escalating blockers with clear options

• Developing high-quality materials, including decks, briefing documents, trackers and status reports

• Supporting change management, including stakeholder mapping, readiness assessments, readiness checklists and manager materials

• Clarifying roles and responsibilities when work crosses teams, and driving quick decisions on who owns what

• Using AI, automation and our People systems to streamline work, speed up reporting and help leaders make faster, better-informed decisions

• Managing intake and prioritization so the People team works on the right things in the right order

• Building templates, trackers and processes that make the team’s work more consistent and easier to run

• Facilitating working sessions and meetings, building toward leading larger discussions with senior leaders

• Defining success metrics for your projects and using data to report on progress and recommend adjustments

• Handling sensitive and confidential information with discretion

Experience:

• 5+ years of experience in project management, program coordination, business operations, HR operations, HR generalist work or consulting

• Track record managing projects or workstreams independently, with a strong eye for detail and follow-through

• Strong written communication and experience building clear, polished materials for leaders

• Experience coordinating across teams and keeping multiple stakeholders aligned

• Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to bring structure to loosely defined work

• Comfort using data to track progress and support recommendations

• Experience running recurring business processes such as planning cycles, OKRs or business reviews is a plus

• Exposure to HR or People functions preferred

• Experience supporting change management or organizational change preferred

• Experience using AI tools and automation to improve how work gets done

Benefits:

• Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled

• Mental health benefits

• Family building benefits

• Child care and pet benefits

• 401(k) plan with company match to help save for your future

• In addition to 12 observed holidays, salaried team members have discretionary paid time off, hourly team members have 15 days paid time off

• 18 weeks of paid parental leave. Biological, adoptive, and foster parents are all eligible

• Subsidized commuter benefits

• Monthly Lyft credits and complimentary Lyft Pink membership

Lyft is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other basis prohibited by law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable federal, state and local law.

Lyft highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture. This role will be in-office on a hybrid schedule following the establishment of a Lyft office in Nashville — Team Members will be expected to work in the office 3 days per week on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. Lyft considers working in the office at least 3 days per week to be an essential function of this hybrid role. jobs.title: Lead Partnerships Manager, Development and Innovation
jobs.description:
Persons in these roles are expected to work from our offices in Seattle. On-site requirements vary based on position and team. If you have questions about on-site work arrangements for this role, please ask your recruiter.

Our base salary range is $166,000 - $250,000, and in addition we have generous bonus plans to provide a competitive compensation package.

Who You Are:

You use a combination of empathy and analytical skills to quickly assess whether a potential partnership has legs. After a couple of conversations with a new organization, you have a working view of what each side would actually get, who inside their org can decide, and what it would take to get there — and you are as willing to recommend passing as pursuing. You are proactive and clear in communicating what you learn. A memo or a short proposal from you is something a researcher, a general counsel, and a program manager can each act on. You are not primarily a door opener; the value you add is in the thinking and the follow-through.

You are at home in the room with researchers and engineers, and you follow AI closely and can hold a credible conversation with technical staff at a frontier lab. You are just as comfortable speaking with a field practitioner or a program officer, and you can describe what Ai2 builds in terms each of them recognizes.

You like building the system as much as working it. You’ll develop how Ai2 approaches partnership pipeline management going forward, including the prioritization framework, and informing the criteria we use to decide which opportunities to pursue. Ai2 runs lean, and you’ll own the work end to end, from initial outreach and tracking to follow-through.

Who We Are:

At Ai2, our mission is to develop breakthrough AI that solves the world’s biggest problems. We believe the insight needed to get there lives at the intersection of deep scientific AI understanding and applying AI in common-good domains. This role is part of our reinvigorated partnerships function and will sit on our Strategic Programs team, which also includes Product Management, Design, and Communications. As a team, we help shape Ai2’s strategic vision and accelerate execution of its goals. We are a highly collaborative team with a high bar for excellence, and we aren’t afraid to question how things have been done in the past to propose changes that drive the organization forward. It’s a very exciting time to be part of this team as Ai2 plays a unique role in shaping how AI changes the world.

Your Next Challenge:

At Ai2, our mission is to develop breakthrough AI that solves the world’s biggest problems. We believe the insight needed to get there lives at the intersection of deep scientific AI understanding and applying AI in common-good domains. This role is part of our reinvigorated partnerships function and will sit on our Strategic Programs team, which also includes Product Management, Design, and Communications. As a team, we help shape Ai2’s strategic vision and accelerate execution of its goals. We are a highly collaborative team with a high bar for excellence, and we aren’t afraid to question how things have been done in the past to propose changes that drive the organization forward. It’s a very exciting time to be part of this team as Ai2 plays a unique role in shaping how AI changes the world.

The essential functions include, but are not limited to the following:

• Run the hub for translational partnerships: pipeline of opportunities, a prioritization framework, and a regular cadence with the partnership owners embedded in Ai2’s program teams.

• Take intro meetings with prospective partners, assess the opportunity, and recommend an approach and a priority, including recommending that we pass.

• Develop and apply Ai2’s partnership screen (both initially and ongoing as a partnership evolves) to judge whether a partnership successfully connects our work to real-world use, unlocks funding for a roadmap we already want to pursue, or validates our technology through credible external deployment.

• Write the memos, assessments, and proposals that move a partnership forward, for internal decision-makers and external partners alike.

• Drive early execution on high-priority partnerships when one needs an owner, including standing up and running joint working groups and steering committees.

• In collaboration with senior leadership, scope partnership terms and drive agreements to signature with legal, finance, and grants administration.

• Track the health of the partnership portfolio and make recommendations to deepen, pivot, or wind down, with reporting leadership can read quickly.

• Work with Communications so prospective partners understand what partnering with Ai2 looks like and what we are looking for.

• Represent Ai2 at conferences and events.

What You’ll Need:

• A bachelor’s degree with 12 years of relevant experience, an advanced degree with 8+ years, or a PhD with 5+ years, in business development, partnerships, technology transfer, or strategy, including partnerships you sourced and closed yourself.

• AI fluency to hold a credible conversation with researchers and engineers, and to stay current on where the field is heading. You do not need to have trained a model.

• Understanding of how external entrepreneurial institutions make and fund partnership decisions (sponsors, approvers, budget cycles, legal and procurement), and a track record of moving proposals through them.

• Clear, audience-aware writing: memos, proposals, and assessments that people read and act on.

• Legal and regulatory fluency (IP, grants, funding agreements) to help scope terms and work effectively with legal and grants administration.

• Excellent relationship-building and stakeholder management, with the ability to represent Ai2 credibly to senior leaders, funders, and program leads.

• Comfort operating with ambiguity and building frameworks and processes where none exist yet, without an ops layer behind you.

• Adaptability to learn a new domain quickly, given how broad Ai2’s partner base is.

• Willingness to travel and attend evening events.

Nice To Have:

• Experience in a research organization, national lab, university technology transfer office, or foundation, where timelines and incentives differ from a product company.

• Background in health and biosciences.

• Experience building a partnership function, pipeline, or CRM practice from scratch.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by a team member to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions.

• Must be able to remain in a stationary position for long periods of time.

• The ability to communicate information and ideas so others will understand. Must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.

• The ability to observe details at close range.

• Can work under deadlines.

A Little More About Ai2:

Ai2 is a Seattle based non-profit AI research institute founded in 2014 by the late Paul Allen. Our mission is building breakthrough AI to solve the world’s biggest problems. We develop foundational AI research and innovation to deliver real-world impact through large-scale open models, data, robotics, conservation, and beyond.

In addition to Ai2’s core mission, we also aim to contribute to humanity through our treatment of each member of the Ai2 Team. Some highlights are:

• We are a learning organization – because everything Ai2 does is ground-breaking, we are learning every day. With a wide variety of world-class AI experts as guest speakers, and our commitment to your personal on-going education, Ai2 is a place where you will have opportunities to continue learning alongside your coworkers.

• We value diversity - We seek to hire, support, and promote people from all genders, ethnicities, and all levels of experience regardless of age. We particularly encourage applications from women, non-binary individuals, people of color, members of the LGBTQA+ community, and people with disabilities of any kind.

• We value inclusion - We understand the value that people's individual experiences and perspectives can bring to an organization, and we are building a culture in which all voices are heard, respected and considered.

• We emphasize a healthy work/life balance – we believe our team members are happiest and most productive when their work/life balance is optimized. While we value powerful research results which drive our mission forward, we also value dinner with family, weekend time, and vacation time. We offer generous paid vacation and sick leave as well as family leave.

• We are collaborative and transparent – we consider ourselves a team, all moving with a common purpose. We are quick to cheer our successes, and even quicker to share and jointly problem solve our failures.

• We are in Seattle – and our office is on the water! We have mountains, we have lakes, we have four seasons, we bike to work, we have a vibrant theater scene, and we have so much else. We welcome interest from applicants from outside of the United States.

• We are friendly– chances are you will like every one of the 200+ (and growing) people who work here. We do.

Ai2 is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. You may view the related Know Your Rights compliance poster and the Pay Transparency Nondiscrimination Provision by clicking on their corresponding links.

This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. If E-Verify cannot confirm that you are authorized to work, this employer is required to give you written instructions and an opportunity to contact the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so you can begin to resolve the issue before the employer can take any action against you, including terminating your employment. Employers can only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to employees and applicants with disabilities to the full extent required by the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). If you feel you need a reasonable accommodation pursuant to the ADA, you are encouraged to contact us at recruiting@allenai.org.

Benefits:

• Team members and their families are covered by medical, dental, vision, and an employee assistance program.

• Team members are able to enroll in our health savings account plan, our healthcare reimbursement arrangement plan, and our health care and dependent care flexible spending account plans.

• Team members are able to enroll in our company’s 401k plan.

• Team members will receive $125 per month to assist with commuting or internet expenses and will also receive $200 per month for fitness and wellbeing expenses.

• Team members will also receive up to ten sick days per year, up to seven personal days per year, up to 20 vacation days per year and twelve paid holidays throughout the calendar year.

• Team members will be able to receive annual bonuses and can participate in the long-term incentive plan.

Note: This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the team members(s) of this position. Team members will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related duties requested by any person authorized to give instructions or assignments. All duties and responsibilities are essential functions and requirements and are subject to possible modification to reasonably accommodate individuals with disabilities. To perform this job successfully, the team member(s) will possess the skills, aptitudes, and abilities to perform each duty proficiently. Some requirements may exclude individuals who pose a direct threat or significant risk to the health or safety of themselves or others. The requirements listed in this document are the minimum levels of knowledge, skills, or abilities. Our Values

Belonging: We celebrate our differences. We support each other and we always stand together.​

Diversity & Inclusion

Fairmont is committed to creating an inclusive environment where diverse talent thrives. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds to join our team.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.
